recipes.title: Ema's Moroccan Meat Patties with Celery and Peas

items.text: Orlee is a pro at this by now. She uses frozen peas. She says that if you do this, you need to put the peas in with the celery when you cook them, because the frozen peas take longer to cook than non-frozen peas. Normally you start cooking the non-frozen peas later than the celery.
Ema says Moroccans overcook their peas because they taste better that way.
Dutch oven / sauté pan with high top
2-3 cubes of frozen sautéed onions, defrosted (if you don't have it, dice 1 medium onion and sauté it till nice and brown)
1/4 cup breadcrumbs or 3 slices of chopped challah bread (Ema uses gluten-free Katz's)
2 T olive oil or coconut oil for frying
2 heads of celery, cut into 1/2in - 1in chunks
2-3 cubes of frozen sautéed onions (if you don't have it, dice 1 medium onion and sauté it till nice and brown)
1 can of peas, drained (if you don't like peas, leave them out) OR one small package of frozen peas, defrosted
1 tablespoon of honey, drizzled on top
Mix meat patty ingredients together (except for olive oil) and form meat patties in medium size

Place olive oil into pan, heat up, and cook meat patties on medium high until brown crust forms on each side. They do not need to be fully cooked at this point. Ema says: don't let meat patties hang out alone, they get lonely (i.e. don't let them burn)
Add cut up celery and the other 2-3 cubes of frozen sautéed onions to the pan with the meat patties
Add 1-2 cups of water (not too much, just so that everything doesn't burn)
Add 1 tsp salt, 1/2-1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2-1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp dried parsley flakes
Lightly mix spices into ingredients (try no to break meat patties)
Cover pan, put flame on very low, and cook ingredients until celery is soft (about 10 minutes)
Open can of drained peas and add to pot
Lightly mix food (try no to break meat patties)
Cook until peas heated through (about ten minutes more, still on very low flame)

photos.caption: Ema made this again and sent more pics

recipes.summary: Orlee is a pro at this by now.

recipes.title: Savta's Sweet n' Sour Meatballs

items.text: Matzo meal or panko (I use some old challah soaked in water and squeezed till all water removed)
2 or 3 cups of water for the sauce, depending on how much sauce you want or how thick you want it to be.
Mix all meatball ingredients in a large bowl.
Combine sauce ingredients in a soup pot. Bring sauce to a boil.
Form meat balls. Place into boiling sauce, cook for about an hour or until burned.
If it tastes lousy, start all over again and use your recipe!

recipes.title: Ema's Dagim for Shabbat (Whitefish and Flounder)

items.text: Ema normally cooks the fish eggs and regular fish simultaneously, in different pots.
1 bunch of parsley, stems removed, chopped
1 bunch of cilantro, stems removed, chopped
Mild olive oil (Gefen brand with purple label)
6 baby peppers OR 1/2 red pepper and 1/2 green pepper, sliced
4 whitefish and/or 6 medium flounder fillets (no bones). You can add more or less - Note: if anything smells fishy, let fish sit in lemon or lime water (squeeze about 1 lemon/lime)

Wash parsley and cilantro. Let cilantro sit in bowl of water for a few minutes because it has a lot of dirt in it. The dirt will eventually fall to the bottom. Cut off the off parsley and cilantro stems, remove all the hard piece. Chop the leaves.
Pour mild olive oil into pot until it covers the bottom. About a cup or more, depending on pan size.
To the pot, add cilantro, parsley, tomatoes and peppers.
Cook uncovered on medium high for 5-10 minutes. Don't want anything to burn.
Add 1 cup of water, 2 tsp salt, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric.
Wash whitefish, dip both sides into sauce, place into pot. Put it in before flounder. Needs more time to cook.
Sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon salt on each whitefish.
Cover and cook for five minutes on low.
Uncover pot, dip both sides of flounder into sauce. Don't add salt - it's too thin and doesn't need it.
Check amount of water in pot. If looks like its getting dry, add 1/2 cup of water to fish (Fish eggs can get 1 full cup).
Cook covered on low for 20 minutes.
If it's still too watery, uncover and let it cook on medium till thick (a few minutes). Every now and then spoon sauce onto fish.

photos.caption: If too thin, cook uncovered for longer

recipes.summary: Ema normally cooks the fish eggs and regular fish simultaneously, in different pots.

recipes.title: Ema's Jasmine Rice

items.text: 4 cups hot water (so takes shorter time to boil)
2 sprinkles paprika (don't want it to be too red)
2 cups of jasmine rice (DON'T ADD with above ingredients
Add all ingredients EXCEPT jasmine rice to a medium sized rice pot.
Bring to boil again (because when you add the rice, it stops boiling).
Option 1: Bring heat down to low, cook for 20 minutes (make sure rice doesn't overflow), after 20 minutes remove from fire, wait five minutes, then uncover, and mix rice.
Option 2: Let boil for five minutes (make sure rice doesn't overflow), shut flame, let it sit covered on stove for 40 minutes. Then uncover, mix ONE time (if you mix more it will get starchy).
Taste to see if it needs more salt.
I suggest you eat this with Ema's lamb stew.
if the rice overflows, lower heat a little.

recipes.summary: With hot water, turmeric, parsley flakes & sprinkles paprika.

recipes.title: Ema's Moroccan Lamb Stew

items.text: 4 cubes of frozen sautéed onions (if you don't have it, dice 1 large onion and sauté it till nice and brown)
2 T of olive oil or coconut oil
8 oz small can of plain tomato sauce (NOT pasta sauce)
1 cup of chicken or beef broth
1/4 cup halved dried apricots (apricots are very sweet, so a little goes a long way)
Place oil into pan, heat up on high, put lamb into pan and brown ALL sides.
Lower heat to medium-low (because you don't want anything to burn).
Put sautéed onions into pan and heat them through so that they melt (if you're using the frozen ones).

Add the rest of the ingredients into the pot (tomato sauce, tomatoes, garbanzo beans, chicken or beef broth, dried apricots, dried prunes, salt, turmeric, parsley flakes, paprika, garlic powder, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, and cilantro).
Mix ingredients, cover pot, reduce heat to low, cook for 1.5- 2 hours.

recipes.summary: With lamb stew meat, frozen sautéed onions, olive oil & plain tomato sauce.

recipes.title: Ema's Shabbat Beitzei Dagim (Fish Eggs)

items.text: Note: Ema normally cooks the fish eggs and regular fish simultaneously, in different pots. You can add the fish eggs into the dagim, but be sure to check with Ema about the process, because fish eggs cook for longer than dagim and need more water.
1 bunch of parsley, stems removed, chopped
1 bunch of cilantro, stems removed, chopped
Mild olive oil (Gefen brand with purple label)
6 baby peppers OR 1/2 red pepper and 1/2 green pepper, sliced
Dev-vein and clean the fish eggs. It's disgusting, but it has to be done or the fish eggs will be bitter. If you see anything yellow, remove it and anything around it. That's the bile from the liver.

Wash parsley and cilantro. Let cilantro sit in bowl of water for a few minutes because it has a lot of dirt in it. The dirt will eventually fall to the bottom. Cut off the off parsley and cilantro stems, remove all the hard piece. Chop the leaves.
Pour mild olive oil into pot until it covers the bottom. About a cup or more, depending on pan size.
To the pot, add cilantro, parsley, tomatoes, peppers, 2 tsp salt, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric.
Cook uncovered on medium high for 5-10 minutes. Don't want anything to burn.
Add 1 cup of water, 2 tsp salt, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric.
Cover, cook for five minutes. (Until this point, it's the same recipe for the dagim. So if you're cooking dagim and fish eggs at the same time, it's the same process for both pots)
Add 1 cup water. They eat up a lot of water.
Cook covered on low for 30 minutes. Keep checking to make sure it's not burning. After about 10 minutes, split fish eggs into chunks if they had cooked into one big block.

photos.caption: The right side is what the cleaned eggs should look like
Ema cooks the fish eggs in the small pot and the dagim in the big pot
Sliced tomatoes, peppers and oil in pot
Add more water. Once fish eggs cook enough, break them up into chunks if they're stuck all together

recipes.summary: Ema normally cooks the fish eggs and regular fish simultaneously, in different pots.

recipes.title: Ema's Simple Sweet Potato Medallions

items.text: 3 large sweet potatoes, cut into round (about 1/4 - 1/2 in thick)
About 4 T honey (or just squeeze three lines of honey on each medallions)
Mix potatoes with olive oil and salt.
Spread on a large cookie sheet.
Squeeze three lines of honey on each round.
Bake on 350 for an hour and a half.

recipes.summary: With sweet potatoes, olive oil & honey.

recipes.title: Ema's Almond Joy Balls

items.text: 1/4 cup semidark chocolate (you can use milk chocolate or dark chocolate if you want
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spread the almonds on a baking sheet and bake in preheated oven for about 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, stir together the corn syrup, powdered sugar, melted butter, coconut extract, shredded coconut and vanilla extract, to form a thick paste.
Moisten hands slightly and form mixture into small balls. Place on a pan or parchment paper.
In a medium, microwave-safe bowl, melt chocolate by microwaving it for 15 seconds, then stirring, microwaving for 15 seconds, then stirring, etc. until it's smooth and melty.
Drizzle melted chocolate onto the coconut bal. Sprinkle with almonds.
Allow to cool at room temperature until chocolate hardens, or freeze.

recipes.summary: With slivered almonds, corn syrup, powdered sugar & melted margarine.

recipes.title: Ema's Minute Roast

items.text: Ema makes this on Shabbos a lot and it's DA BOMB
1 T salt (add more to taste later)
6 tsp prepared chopped garlic, or 8 cloves of sliced garlic
In a small bowl combine onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and dried parsley and mix them. Add garlic and mix. Then add ketchup and sugar, mix.
In a roasting pan layer half of the sliced onions, and half of the sauce on top.
Place the roast on top, and then layer the rest of the onions and sauce.
Bake at 375 for half hour and then at 325 for 3 - 3 1/2 hours (meat should be very soft).
When cooled remove the heat from the sauce, slice and place in a new pan. Pour sauce over meat, warm and serve.
If you find that the minute roast is too hard after you cut it, you can put it back into the oven at 350 in its own sauce.

photos.caption: Sliced meat put back into sauce

recipes.summary: Ema makes this on Shabbos a lot and it's DA BOMB

Optional 1/2 tsp sugar (Ema's secret ingredient - I had no idea either)
Cut off white part inside of cabbage, remove thick outside layers
Cut up cabbage into chucks that will fit into food processor
Grind cabbage in in food processor into medium-small pieces (see picture of blade)
Place ground cabbage into big mixing bowl

items.text: 4-6 green, red or yellow peppers (Abba likes red), Ema likes to use mini peppers these days
1 lb of ground beef or ground dark turkey
3 squares of frozen fried onions OR 1 grated onion
1/4 tsp of black pepper (omit if making this for Abba)
3 squares frozen fried onions OR 1 onion chopped
NEW recipes: 15 ounce can of tomato sauce and about 3/4 of a cup of water

2-3 T sugar (depending on how sweet you want it)

Pour sauce over the peppers. Make sure some sauce stays on top of the peppers.

recipes.title: Ema's Mini Meatballs with Olives

items.text: You can make this recipe without the meatballs, just as an olive side dish. See below.
2 cans of greed pitted olives, drained
3 squares of frozen sautéed onions, defrosted (or 1 sautéed onion)
3 slices of challah bread (Ema uses gluten-free Katz's)
Fill up saucepan 3/4 full with water.

Add 15 oz can of tomato sauce, half tablespoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon of dried parsley, 1 teaspoon of honey, 1/2 teaspoon of soy sauce, one can of water.
Place on medium flame and prepare meat mixture.

bring to a boil and immediately lower flame to low.

recipes.title: Fricase ala Emil/Chanofsky

items.text: "This recipe is really Bubby Bertha's recipe Z'L...She made fricassee on Friday nights and for Yom Tovim. We always had fricassee as an opener. At that time giblets were the cheapest parts of the chicken and therefore the food of choice for a special occasion like Shabbat."
"Amounts are questionable, so don't hold me to it. Frankly, it doesn't matter if you're off a bit. This recipe serves 20 +-. Cut down ingredients for a first try or for smaller groups."
Savta often makes her fricase as an appetizer on Pesach.
Fun fact: Abba doesn't often swing Ashki, but when he does, he goes for Savta's fricase.
For all of you who don't remember, Emil is Savta's maiden name.
4 cloves garlic, chopped (can use frozen or fresh)
2 lbs meat balls (as per my sweet n' sour meatball recipe)
Matzo meal or panko (I use some old challah soaked in water and squeezed till all water removed)
In a large pot saute the onions and garlic until onions have softened.
After the onions have softened add spices. Then add boiling water.
When all ingredients are thoroughly mixed, put the meat ingredients into the boiling water and then prepare the meatballs in ping pong ball sizes.
Add the meatballs and make certain they are covered with liquid. Add more boiling water if necessary.
Cook on a medium flame for about 1 1/2 hours or longer.
Check to make sure that the water has not boiled out.

recipes.title: Ema's Mac and Cheese

items.text: Large pot to cook rue (if you cook the macaroni and set it aside first, you can use the same put for the rue).

1 package macaroni (Ema uses gluten free and only the Tinkyada brand)

6 slices American cheese (Ema uses the white kind. Also, Ema can't eat the orange kind because the Anatto)
2 T flour OR 1 T potato starch (dissolved in 1 T cold water)
Cook macaroni according to package, rinse in cold water, drain it, set aside. DO NOT overcook the gluten free kind, it won't be good.
In a large pit, bring milk to boil and immediately lower flame to low.
Add in garlic powder, parsley, turmeric, salt, paprika, honey, onion powder, optional ground black pepper, optional Sriracha
If you want a thick rue, mix in 1 tablespoon flour OR 1 tablespoon potato starch (dissolved in 1 T cold water)
After everything is mixed and hot, lower flame to low, and add in the macaroni.

recipes.title: Ema's Couscous

items.text: Eitan tested this recipe. He said it was good, but it needed less salt. I changed the salt measurements as a result.

On the kfar (village in Israel) and in Morocco, the women made Couscous every Friday afternoon (not for Shabbat). They did this so that when their families came to wish them shabbat shalom, everyone had something to eat. Coucous is a great dish for when people are coming in and out of the house because it can feed a lot of people and you can stretch it. Doda Sara still does this on Friday. Abba would love for us all to continue this tradition and eat Coucous as a family on Friday afternoon before Shabbat.
In our family couscous is a must on Chanukkah and Succot.
The whole family and many, many more people
Largest pot you have - if you don't have a huge one, buy one. If you want to make less couscous, you'll have to figure out a new recipe on your own.
6 full chicken legs, with thighs and drumsticks
1 T salt (maybe less, put in half and then add more as needed)
2 packages butternut squash cubes (about 1 medium butternut squash) OR pumpkin
1/2 package of baby carrots OR three large carrots cubed
2 turnips, peeled and cuzt into chunks
Optional 3 cubes of frozen fried onion (or 1 sautéed, chopped onion)
30-40 oz of couscous (about 4 boxes of couscous) - make sure it's instant and not the egg barley kind. NOT Israeli couscous

In order to make the broth, fill half of the pot up with water. Add chicken legs and broth spices/flavorings (salt, onion powder, garlic powder, parsley flakes, turmeric, paprika, honey, soy sauce, black pepper and Sriracha).
Let boil for 10-15 minutes. Cut the veggies now, if you haven't already and sauté onion if you don't have frozen cubes (you can omit this if you don't want to sauté them).
Add butternut squash, carrots, zucchini, turnips, cabbages and onions. This will stop the water from boiling. Bring to boil and immediately lower flame to medium.
Cook for about 20 more minutes. (make sure to watch the pot every now and then so nothing boils over).
While broth is cooking, put 30-40 oz of couscous into 9x13 aluminum pan.
Add couscous spices (salt, turmeric, garlic powder, parsley flakes)
Slowly add 1 cup hot water, stopping and mixing in between pours.
Then mix the water into the couscous with your hands, until the water is totally absorbed and there are no chunks of couscous.
Add in can of chickpeas, water drained. Mix.
Add about 2 cups of juice from the boiling couscous (should have boiled for at least 20 minutes). The hot water will cook the couscous. Keep mixing so couscous gets fluffy.
Doda Clodine taught Ema that should put the coucous mixture in the over for 6 minutes to make it fluffy
To serve, mound couscous on large plate and surround with vegetable and chicken. Pour broth sauce on top.

recipes.summary: On the kfar (village in Israel) and in Morocco, the women made Couscous every Friday afternoon (not for Shabbat).

recipes.title: Ema's Baked Potato Rounds

items.text: A large mixing bowl (to mix potatoes into spices and oil)
About 15 yellow golden potatoes, peeled (about 1 bag of them - other potatoes won't taste as good)
1/4 cup oil (you can even add a little less - too much oil will cause the potatoes to get mushy and they won't crisp up when baking)
Ema used to add water to her potatoes, but now she says it's better without the water
Peel and slice potatoes 1/4 inch wide (see picture for reference).
Mix oil and spices onto potatoes (Ema mixes by pouring potatoes into back and forth between two aluminum pans).
Grease cookie sheet with cooking spray
Spread potatoes onto cookie sheet. Ideally all the potatoes are touching bottom of cookie sheet. (Use another cookie sheet if necessary. Ema doesn't go too crazy about this. See pics below.)
Bake at 350 for an hour and a half.

recipes.summary: Ema used to add water to her potatoes, but now she says it's better without the water

recipes.title: Ema's Baked Schnitzel

items.text: Large cookie sheet, greased with cooking spray
2 9x13 aluminum pan (one for egg wash and one for coating)
6 white chicken breast (Preferably the thick types of chicken breast - sometimes they sell them thin)
1 cup Gluten free Matzo meal (Yehuda brand)
Mix coating ingredients in an aluminum pan.
Mix egg wash ingredients in a different aluminum pan.
Dip one piece of chicken in egg wash and then in the breading.
Place breaded chicken onto cookie sheet.
Repeat with the rest of the chicken.
Liberally spray breaded chicken with cooking spray (if you don't spray the chicken very liberally, it will be dry when it comes out of the oven.)

recipes.summary: With white chicken breast, crumb coating, corn flake crumbs & gluten free Matzo meal.

recipes.title: Ema's Crispy Fried Schnitzel

items.text: 2 9x13 aluminum pan (one for egg wash and one for coating)
6 white chicken breast (Preferably the thick types of chicken breast - sometimes they sell them thin)
Olive oil and 2 or 3 T of coconut oil for frying (coconut oil raises the smoke point and the oil won't burn)
1 cup Gluten free Matzo meal (Yehuda brand)
Mix coating ingredients in an aluminum pan.
Mix egg wash ingredients in a different aluminum pan.
Heat up oil in frying pan on medium high flame (approximately 1/2 - 1 in high. You want most of the chicken to be covered).
Dip one piece of chicken in egg wash and then in the breading.
Place breaded chicken onto cookie sheet.
Repeat with the rest of the chicken.
To see if the oil is hot enough put a small piece of chicken into the oil and see if it sizzles.
When the oil is hot enough, place the breaded chicken into the pan.
Fry chicken until the outside is golden brown.
When the chicken is ready, place on paper towels in a pan or a plate)

recipes.summary: With white chicken breast, olive oil and 2, crumb coating & corn flake crumbs.

recipes.title: Yatti's Pomegranate Mint-Relish/Chutney

items.text: Large bowl to seed the pomegranate
Mixing bowl for relish (small to medium)
Apron (seeding pomegranate can get really messy)
1 T red wine vinegar (DON'T replace with other kinds of vinegar - only use red wine)
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh mint (add more or less to taste)
1/4 tsp salt (or more to taste - haven't quite gotten the measurement down yet)

Seed pomegranates. In order to do this, place knife into the peel of the pomegranate and cut a circle around the pomegranate peel. Don't go too deep or you will break the seeds. Then you will be able to break apart the fruit. It will take a bit of twisting. Then you can either pull out individual seeds or you can tap the peel of the fruit with a wooden spoon to make the seeds fall out. Remove the white pieces from around the pomegranate.
Chop shallot and mint. Grate lemon zest.
Combine pomegranate seeds, shallot, oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, vinegar, mint, salt and peper in a bowl.
Cover and chill. Eat soon after it's chilled.
The relish WITHOUT mint can be made 1 day ahead. The mint in the salad goes bad really fast.

recipes.summary: With pomegranates, shallot, olive oil & finely grated lemon zest.

recipes.title: Ema's Fennel Leek Soup

items.text: A few shots of soy sauce
Optional for garnish - 1 extra leek, sliced lengthwise into narrow strips
Optional for garnish - 1/4 green pepper, diced
Heat 2 T olive oil in a large saucepan; add fennel and leek. Sauté for 5 minutes. Add stock, dill, onions, rosemary, honey, soy sauce, onion powder, garlic powder and salt.
Cook, covered, over medium heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove rosemary. Purée the soup with an immersion blender. Reheat soup and season with salt if necessary.
For garnish: heat 1 T oil in frying pan; cook extra leek and green pepper 3 to 5 minutes until soft, but not browned.
Spoon soup into bowls and top with fried leek and green pepper.

recipes.summary: With olive oil, fennel bulbs, leaks & vegetable stock.

recipes.title: Ema's Chicken with Wax Beans

items.text: 6 cans of waxbeans (one can per person), drained

Place oil into pan, heat up and brown chicken on both sides. If you don't want to use oil, heat up a cup of water and cook the outside of the chicken on both sides. Watch it constantly and turn it over when one side gets done outwardly. This is not to cook it inside, only to braise it outside.
Add spices, two cups to three cups of water. Mix.

When you cook it, keep it covered but slightly open so that it doesn't overflow from the steam. If it has too much water after a half-hour, uncover it and let the water cook out but leave enough so that there's a sauce.

recipes.summary: With waxbeans, chicken legs, plain tomato sauce & garlic powder.

recipes.title: Ema's Meat Stuffed Artichoke Hearts

items.text: Ema made this again cuz she forgot the recipe was already here. Merge two recipes and PITCUREs
I didn’t see this on the blog and I just made it so here it is.
Three 9X13 inch pans aluminum foil or other). (You might want to put another pan underneath each one keep it stable.)
One large bowl for mixing meat
One large pot for boiling artichokes
Three packages of frozen artichoke hearts
One and a half pounds of chopped meat
1/4 cup matzo meal (can use gluten-free matzo meal), optional (makes it softer)
3 cubes of frozen fried onions, defrosted
1–2 teaspoons of Cumin (depending upon how you like it)
Hot Water (from sink) for pan,about an inch of water for 9 x 13 pan
Lemon juice from One lemon, squeezed
2-3 cubes of frozen fried onions, defrosted
About a tablespoon of honey drizzled on each pan, optional
Meat mixture (same one that Ema uses for miniature meatballs with olives)
3 squares of frozen sautéed onions, defrosted (or 1 sautéed onion)
3 slices of challah bread (Ema uses gluten-free Katz's)
3 squares of frozen sautéed onions, defrosted (or 1 sautéed onion)
Boil artichokes in a large pot of water for about 45 to 50 minutes or until soft. Remove from water and cool (on a large pan).
Put all of sauce ingredients in one 9x13 pan and mix well.
In a large bowl, put all ingredients for meat mixture. Mix well with gloved hands or with a large spoon.

Lay out artichokes on two 9 x 13” pan’s. Using a tablespoon, mound the meat into each artichoke heart and put a little extra in to account for shrinkage when heated. After all the hearts are filled, pour half of the sauce over the artichoke hearts in one pan and the other half over the hearts in the other pan. Cover with silver foil and bake in oven for about 45 to 15 minutes. Unwrap and serve as an appetizer or as a side dish.
Boil a pot of water, place frozen artichoke hearts into it. Cook for 20 minutes, or until soft. Check if soft by poking with fork. May need longer or shorter boiling time.
When the artichokes are ready, remove them from water and place them into aluminum pans.
While the artichokes are cooking, combine meat mixture ingredients in a large mixing bowl. Mush together with your hands.
In a separate pan or bowl, combine the sauce ingredients. Mix.
When the artichokes are ready, create meat balls and stuff the meat mixture into the artichokes. Overstuff the artichokes because they will shrink when cooking.
Pour the sauce that you made into the stuffed artichoke pans.
After you pour the sauce, drizzle artichokes with honey.
Large mixing bowl (for sauce - Ema uses an aluminum pan)

recipes.title: Ema's Rock Cornish Hens (Baby Chicken)

items.text: Large aluminum pan with tall sides
Place chickens into pan, pour salt, garlic powder, parsley, turmeric, paprika and olive oil onto chicken and mush around so they're evenly distributed.
Pour honey on top of chicken.
Bake covered at 325 for 1 1/2 - 2 hours. After that, uncover and cook at 375 for ten minutes.

recipes.summary: With rock cornish hens, garlic powder, dried parsly flakes & turmeric.

recipes.title: Abba's Tzalmelah (Paprika Sauce for Fried Fish)

items.text: We always eat this with fried and baked breaded fish.
Abba traditionally pours so much tzalmelah on his fried fish that he makes a mabool (flood).
Tzalmelah is sometimes referred to as charmoula, but Abba thinks that sounds funny.
3 T paprika (you can add more if you want)
Juice of 2 lemons (you can add more if you want)
1 tsp salt - edit: maybe put in 1/2 tsp first and then see if it needs more
1/2 cup of water (maybe a little less of a little more - use your judgment. If it's to thick put in more paprika)
Mix together all the ingredients EXCEPT water. The consistency should be pasty.
Add water slowly. Check the consistency. You want it to be a little loose, but not too watery.
Always ALWAYS eat with Ema's baked or fried breaded fish.
Pour on fish - make a mabool

recipes.summary: We always eat this with fried and baked breaded fish.

recipes.title: Abba's Tznon (Radishes)

items.text: Only Abba eats these. Sometimes Tantan takes a bite or two, when he's feeling extra Moroccan.
Part of the Shabbat salad spread. They're odd, like the fennel recipe, but it works.

items.text: Same recipe as Ema's baked schnitzel

Mix coating ingredients in an aluminum pan.

Dip one piece of fish in egg wash and then in the breading.
Place breaded fish onto cookie sheet.

recipes.title: Ema's Dag Metugan (Fried Fish)

items.text: Same recipe as fried schnitzel, just with fish
2 9x13 aluminum pan (one for egg wash and one for coating)
Olive oil and 2 or 3 T of coconut oil for frying (coconut oil raises the smoke point and the oil won't burn)
1 cup Gluten free Matzo meal (Yehuda brand)
Mix coating ingredients in an aluminum pan.
Mix egg wash ingredients in a different aluminum pan.
Heat up oil in frying pan on medium high flame (approximately 1/2 - 1 in high. You want most of the fish to be covered).
Dip one piece of fish in egg wash and then in the breading.
Place breaded fish onto cookie sheet.
Repeat with the rest of the fish.
To see if the oil is hot enough put a small piece of fish into the oil and see if it sizzles.
When the oil is hot enough, place the breaded fish into the pan.
Fry fish until the outside is golden brown.
When the fish is ready, place on paper towels in a pan or a plate.
Drown the fish in a mabool of tzalmelah.

recipes.title: Ema's Magical Cheese-Sponge Cake

items.text: Stand mixer with attachment to whip egg whites
2 containers lactaid lowfat (1 lb each) cottage cheese
3/4 cup gluten free baking mix (not 100% sure about this)
Blend cottage cheese and pudding in blender until it has a smooth texture, like cream cheese.
Separately, whip 8 egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Put yolks in large bowl and beat with a fork. Add cottage cheese-pudding blend. Add rest of ingredients EXCEPT for egg white. The mixture should be well blended.
Grease bottom (and only the bottom) of bundt pan (pan needs to have high sides).
Depending on pan size, fill it up to 3/4 full only. It will rise.
Bake for 1 hour, until toothpick comes out clean.
Close oven and leave cake there for 1/2 hour.

recipes.title: Ema's Salad Mayonnaise (Potato Salad)

items.text: Typically eaten as part of the Shabbat salad spread
Don't add paprika, it makes the dressing a funny pink color
6 potatoes (Ema does NOT suggest using Yukon Gold potatoes because it makes the salad very mushy. Ideally use baking potatoes, such as Idaho)
About 6 Israeli pickles - either in brine or in vinegar, although Ema likes Vinegar. (You can also replace the Israeli pickles with canned peas.)

Boil potatoes for approximately a half hour or until a fork can be easily inserted in the middle. Do not over-boil because you do not want the potatoes to be mushy. Drain and let cool on a pan, slightly separated. When cooled, peel potatoes. Cut into large cubes.
Boil eggs for 10-12 minutes, util hard boiled. After that, put into cold water so they're easier to peel. Peel eggs and chop them.
Mix the potatoes, eggs and pickles together.
Make the dressing. Combine mayonnaise, salt, garlic powder, turmeric, and optional sugar. Mix. Add water or parve milk. Mix.
Add dressing to potato-egg mixture and gently mix.

recipes.title: Ema's Cherry Almond Gluten-Free Squares

items.text: This can be made dairy or parve
1 package raw all purpose gluten free dough (Katz's brand), defrosted and left out for at least 1/2 hour until soft
1 can cheery cake and pastry filling
3/4 cup of all purpose gluten free flour
4 T low fat parve margarine spread OR butter OR just margarine
Spread dough with finger across pan, make 1/4 inch lip all around edges.
Put dough in oven for 10-15 minutes. Remove from oven and cool slightly.
Beat almond paste well with egg white.
Spread almond paste over cooled crust.
Spread cherry filling evenly over almond paste.
Make topping: mix flour, salt and sugar together. Using hands, mix margarine or butter into the flour mixture until there are coarse crumbs. Gently fold in almond slices.

Bake at 350 for 45 minutes - 1 hour. More if needed. The gluten free flour doesn't get golden brown on top. If you use regular flour and make this non gluten free, you cut the baking time down to 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Ema's Gluten-free Matzo Blintzes (Lactose Reduced Option)

items.text: These can be made for Pesach if you use Matzo
You can also replace the Matzo with saltines. Ema used to use this recipe with saltines and make it for us when we came home from school.
1 1/2 containers of Lactaid low-fat cottage cheese
1 single serving container of vanilla or yogurt (to make it lactose reduced) OR 1/4 sour cream
2 T cream cheese OR mayonnaise (to make it lactose reduced)
1/4 cup sugar (you can use less if you don't want it sweet)
One box of gluten-free matzo OR saltines
Option 1: If you are baking these in the oven, then preheat oven to 350°F. Grease two cookie sheets with Pam spray.
Option 2: If you are frying these then get a large frying pan ready with olive oil and, if you have it, a little bit of coconut oil.
Mix all of filling ingredients in a medium to large bowl until well mixed.
Put the eggs and milk for the matzo/egg ingredients into a wide mouth bowl and mix well.

Take the full matzos and crack them into smaller pieces. Dip the pieces into the egg/milk mixture, then slightly fill them with the filling ingredients. The ingredients should be about a quarter to a half an inch thick depending upon how you like it. Cover the filling with another piece of dipped matzo and create a sandwich.
If you have extra filling left, you can make small latke size rounds and put them either on the baking sheet or fry them.
Option 1: If you are baking, put all of the pieces on a baking sheet and bake them in the oven for about a half hour or until golden on top.

Option 2: If you are frying then heat the oil until it is sizzling, then gently put the pieces in without crowding. When the bottom is golden, gently flip it over and fry the other side until golden. Take out and drain on paper towels.
Eat with syrup, sugar, sour cream or applesauce.

Check the pot and make sure bottom isn't burning.
Add more water if it's cooked out and rice is too hard.

recipes.title: TanTan and Danish's Fantabulous Cilantro Lime Chicken

items.text: Best when made on Monday nights... really makes Mondays easier, you know.
pinch of crushed red pepper flakes

Make marinade: Whisk together 2 tablespoons olive oil, cilantro, lime juice, red pepper flakes, garlic, and cumin. Add chicken and toss to evenly coat with the marinade. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.
When you’re ready to cook the chicken, preheat oven to 425 degrees F.

Pour olive oil into a large oven-proof skillet to cover the bottom of the pan. Heat over medium-high heat. Season both sides of marinated chicken with salt and pepper. Add chicken skin-side down and pour in the marinade. Sear until the skin becomes golden and crispy, about 6 minutes. Flip the chicken thighs, and cook for 2 minutes more. (Chicken should not yet be cooked through).
Turn off the heat and transfer pan into hot oven; bake until the chicken is cooked through, about 10 to 12 minutes more. Be EXTRA CAREFUL when you take the hot pan out of the oven. No joke.
Serve with white rice and drizzle with extra pan drippings.
Drizzle with sriracha if you're feeling jazzy.

recipes.title: Ema's Apricot Onion Chicken

items.text: Boneless chicken breasts , cut into strips (Ema used a family pack of 5 1/2 pounds)

In a large Dutch oven, on medium high heat, put six cubes of frozen sautéed onions. Add to that 2 cups of chicken broth. Now add 1teaspoon each of salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, parsley flakes (dried) and soy sauce. Add 1/2 teaspoon Tumerick and 1 tablespoon of light Caesar dressing (Optional). Heat until it starts to boil and then lower the heat to medium for 10 minutes. Uncovered.

Now add a bunch of boneless chicken breasts ( Ema used a family pack of 5 1/2 pounds). I cut them into thin strips but you can cut them into cubes or leave them whole. I would suggest cutting them somewhat instead of leaving them whole, though.

Bring to a boil and then lower the heat to medium low. After about 10 minutes flip the chicken over, and cook for another 10 minutes. After that, close the fire and cover the chicken just to make sure that it will be totally cooked inside as well as outside.

Now, take a 9 x 13 pan or an aluminum foil pan that you want and take out the chicken but leave the sauce in the pan. To that sauce, add 1 tablespoon of potato starch mixed with 1 tablespoon of water, then mixed with another half cup of water. Put the fire on low and add the potato starch water mixture to the sauce in the pan. Cook for about five minutes while mixing constantly. The sauce should thicken. If it gets too thick add a little more water without potato starch. Now pour the sauce over the chicken in the aluminum pan. Mix well.
At this point you can freeze it (Cover with two layers of silver foil) or you can eat it over a bed of rice. Yum Yum Yum.

recipes.summary: With boneless chicken breasts, frozen fried onion squares, dried parsley & paprika.

recipes.title: Ema's Chicken with Peas and Potatoes

items.text: 4 large or 6 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
Put 2 full chicken legs in a dutch oven on medium high heat and add turmeric, dried parsley flake, paprika, salt, garlic powder, 3 sautéed frozen onion cubes.
Then add about 2 cups of water to cover the bottom but not too deeply.
Cook for about 5 minutes then flip over and cook another 5. Lower heat and cook covered for 10 minutes checking to make sure there is enough water.
Meanwhile peel about 4 large or 6 medium potatoes and cut into wedges. Add to pan.
Add 1 T honey and 1/2 can - 1 can of peas depending on your preference. I add another teaspoon of salt (because potatoes and root vegetables gobble up salt) but you can wait and add more to taste.

Cover and cook on LOW for 40 minutes checking every 10 minutes and to make sure it's not in need of water. If so, add 1/2 cup at a time. Also, mix gently each time so as not to mush the potatoes. Enjoy!

recipes.summary: With full chicken legs, turmeric, dried parsley flakes & paprika.

recipes.title: Savta's Cabbage Soup

items.text: This cabbage soup recipe was passed down from Bubby Tziril (Silbershein) to Bubby Bertha (Emil) to Savta Leah (with modifications - of course)
1 lg head of cabbage shredded or chopped (about 7 cups)
1/3 cup lemon juice or 2 fresh lemons
1 - 2 T salt (or more if you like....salt brings out the other flavors. Maybe start with 1T)
1 jar of pasta sauce (I have also used marinara on occasion, if so, use less salt)
Optional: raisins (Savta adds them in depending on her mood)
Place onions and olive oil in 10 qt. pot. Simmer until onions are translucent, place apples on top and then remaining ingredients. Cover with sufficient water above ingredients to make it soup.
Cook for 2 - 3 hours over medium flame until cabbage and ingredients are brown and tasty. Don't burn.....It may be made in a slow cooker for 6 to 8 hours.

recipes.title: Danish's and TanTan's Spectacular Meat Salad

items.text: 2 tomatoes, diced OR cherry tomatoes, sliced in half
1 can of baby corn, drained / canned corn, drained / grilled corn (3-4 stalks)
Optional - 1 can hearts of palm, sliced and drained
Almonds, slivered and toasted (you can buy slivered almonds)
6-8 sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed really small
Honey garlic soy sauce or any similar sauce
Dry rub - rough estimation. TanTan keeps everything about a teaspoon and a half, but varies sometimes because he loves garlic powder etc.
1 1/2 tsp cumin (or a little less if you want)
1 1/2 teaspoons chile powder or cayenne (depending on how spicy you like it, ya dig?)
Chop veggies and gather the ingredients.
Spray a cookie sheet with nonstick cooking spray and spread cubed sweet potatoes onto pan. Sprinkle with a little bit of olive oil, salt and pepper.
If you don't have toasted almonds, place almonds into an aluminum pan, and place in oven for 5-8mins on until they start to brown.
Combine spices for dry rub in a mixing bowl. Mix it real good till the brown sugar doesn't clump anymore.
Rub steak with olive oil, then sprinkle on a generous amount of dry rub (it all crystallizes) on both sides.

Heat up a skillet and cook the steak on high 6-8 min per side. Towards the end of the 6-8, baste each side with honey garlic soy sauce. After both sides are done cooking, baste each side with the honey garlic soy sauce. And vualla! This is the tastiest rub TanTan ever made.
When everything is done cooking, mix all ingredients together and top with TanTan and Danish's Caesar Salad Dressing.

recipes.title: Ema's Chicken with Cauliflower (and Potatoes)

items.text: This makes enough for six people. If you want less, you can cut the recipe in half or in thirds. When the chicken is cooked well, taste to make sure there is enough salt.
Chicken legs (in this recipe Ema used 6), defrosted
2 tsp garlic powder + 1 tsp for later
2 tsp salt + 1 pinch + 1 tsp for later
2 tsp pepper (leave out if making this for Abba)
6 medium potatoes, peeled, and cut into wedges
3 frozen bags of 24 oz, defrosted cauliflower
Put 2 cups of water in a large dutch oven on high heat.
Add garlic powder, 2 tsp salt, 2 tsp pepper, 2 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp onion powder, and frozen sautéed onions. Mix well.
Add chicken legs. Heat for about five minutes on each side. Lower heat to medium.
Add about a tablespoon of honey. Let cook for about 15 minutes covered.
Add to that, six medium potatoes peeled and cut into wedges. Add a pinch or 2 of salt to that.
Mix a little and flip chicken once.
Cook covered for about another 15 minutes checking to make sure that the water has not evaporated. If so add another cup.
Now add to pan three large bags of defrosted cauliflower.
Add 1 tsp of paprika, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, and 1 tsp turmeric.

Lower heat to low and cook covered for about another 15 minutes, checking once to make sure there is enough water. If the mixture looks dry add another half cup. After 15 minutes, open and mix gently, then cover again and cook for another 15 minutes on low.
Serve each person one piece of chicken surrounded by the cauliflower and a few pieces of potato.

recipes.title: Honey Bee's Super Easy Baked Salmon

items.text: Salmon (As much as you want. Orlee normally uses a 6oz fillet.)
BBQ sauce or any sauce you would put on chicken (Or any other kind of topping you want. Sometimes she uses honey mustard.)
Preheat oven to 450 (I know it seems high, but it works out perfectly every time).
Spray an aluminum pan with cooking spray.
Place salmon into pan and pat dry with paper towel to remove extra moisture.
Dump a bunch of sauce on top and spread around salmon.
Bake at 450 for 12-15 minutes (ideally bake at 12 so not overcooked).

recipes.title: TanTan and Danish's Fancy French Onion Soup

items.text: 6 tablespoons Osem Onion Soup Mix (optional or more salt to taste)
In a 4-quart stockpot, sauté onions in butter over medium heat for about 8 minutes, or until caramelized to a nice golden brown, stirring frequently so they don’t burn.
Add wine and continue to sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stirring to keep lumps from forming, add water, onion soup mix, salt and pepper; bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and place a piece of toasted French bread in each.
Top the toast with a slice or two of cheese and broil for 3 minutes, until cheese is browned and bubbly.

recipes.title: Yatti's Baked Salmon Patties

items.text: Optional - Plastic gloves and/or cheese cloth for squeezing water out of salmon
2 large cans of salmon (I use with bones because it's healthier), drained and squeezed of excess water
1 small can sweet corn kernels, drained
1/2 medium or 1 small onion, diced very small
1/2 cup of breadcrumbs (I use a mix of gluten free - see pics below)

Spray cookie sheet with nonstick spray.
Place everything but salmon into mixing bowl.
Then, open cans of salmon and SQUEEZE excess water out of them. You are welcome to use a cheese cloth and plastic gloves to squeeze salmon, but you are welcome to use your hands, too.
Add salmon to bowl, mix all ingredients together.
Form mixture into patties. Place on cookie sheet.
Bake at 450 for 12-15 minutes (stick with 12 first).
Enjoy with lemon juice, ketchup and salad. Eat hot or cold.

recipes.title: Ema's Chicken with Onions

items.text: 1 large package of full chicken legs (Ema's had 5 in it)
4-6 onions, peeled and diced (Ema used two red onions here instead of two large Spanish onions because she didn't have the two large Spanish onions. It came out fine though.)
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
Put chicken in a large dutch oven with 2 cups of water on medium high heat.
Add 2 tsp each of salt, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric, and 1-2 T honey. Mix well and flip over the chicken so that everything is covered with spices.
Cook on each side for about five minutes until each side looks done on the outside.
Reduce heat to medium low and cover. Cook for 15 minutes.
During that time peel the onions and potatoes and cut into small wedges.
After 15 minutes, put those into the pot.
Add one more teaspoon each of garlic powder, salt, paprika and turmeric.
Add another 1 to 2 cups of water depending upon how wide the pan is (the wider the pan, the more water you need because it evaporates more quickly).
Mix the whole pan well leaving the chicken on top so that the onions and potatoes can cook. Cover again and cook on medium low for 45 minutes.
Open the pan and if there is still a lot of water left, Cook for another 10 or 15 minutes until the water becomes thicker but not until the water evaporates. Remember, you need your sauce!
Serve hot with Bread. Yatti will be happy if it's gluten-free :-)

recipes.summary: With full chicken legs, garlic powder, paprika & turmeric.

recipes.title: TanTan's Crack Meat Roll

items.text: Do the meat and veggies get cooked at same time?
Is it rolled like a deli roll?
How long to bake for? How high is oven?
1 green peppers, slivered or dice small
2 eggs, beaten (to create an egg wash)
Remove puff pastry from freezer and let it defrost.
In the meanwhile, make the meat (One lb ground meat) Cut up a green pepper into small squares or slivers. Same thing to an onion.

Heat up a pan, drizzle with a little olive oil (not a lot because the meat will render out the fat) and brown the meat. Add in diced peppers and onions. Sprinkle with spices (the veggies don't have to be cooked till they're brown and sweet - just till the onion and pepper are soft because they will be cooked in the oven). Get it all good and separate by mixing a lot. A little before it's fully cooked take it off the fire and let it cool for a min.

Rub the inside of the puff pastry with Dijon mustard (TanTan likes a lot but Danes doesn't). Note: The honey Dijon that cooks in the Dough, and the zahtar, give the meat such a creamy flavor when cooked in the dough.
Top the meat on the inside middle layer, but don't overstuff because the heat of the meat will expand the dough. Top inside layers with a little more zahtar). Close it up tight on all sides.
Rub with egg wash. Top with a lot of sesame seeds. Sprinkle more zahtar on top of the sesame seeds just for color. It will burn slightly but it bakes into the dough so it's good.

Bake on a rack so that the layer beneath catches the juices, or else the bottom layer will get soggy (which is all good too). Take it out when it's golden brown (TanTan prefers on the darker side for maximum crunch).

P.S. This is the same kind of ground meat recipe used for tacos or stuffed peppers. For stuffed pepper, just make rice in a separate pot, add to meat mixture and then it then cook it all in the peppers.
This recipe is a great substitute for deli roll.

recipes.title: Ema's Famous Tiramisu

items.text: Ema normally makes this parve and gluten free, but it can also be made with dairy and non-gf ingredients.
Pan with large sides (tiramisu has many layers so want the pan to be high)
Ready made yellow cake (You can buy a cake, make a cake mix, or make it from scratch. There are a lot of boxed gluten-free mixes.)
1 box of parve instant vanilla pudding (make sure it's instant)
1/2 bar of good parve chocolate (like Alpine), crushed it into fine pieces or crumbs (Ema uses a small food processor for this)
Some boiling water (to dissolve instant coffee)
3-5 T coffee or chocolate liquor (like Sabra Liquor)
Buy or make one yellow cake (a loaf cake or two round cakes. This time, I made my own gluten-free yellow cake).
Whip one container of parve whipped topping using a stand mixer or beaters until it is slightly whipped then add the vanilla pudding. Now, mix that whole thing until it is thick and totally whipped.
Take chocolate and crush it into fine pieces or crumbs (Ema uses a small food processor).

Now take a large cup and add in 2 tsp of instant coffee with a few tablespoons of boiling water. Mix until coffee is dissolved. Add about three quarters of a cup of cold water. Then add a couple of tablespoons of liquor.

Now time to put it all together: first, cut the yellow cake into slices about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick. Take a loaf pan or a wide loaf pan depending upon how big you want the tiramisu to be. Put a layer of yellowcake pieces on the bottom, then spoon about one third of the coffee/liquor mixture over it. Now cover that with one third of the whip cream mixture. Now spread about a third of the chocolate crumbs on top of that. Repeat another two times. You can spread some cake crumbs over-the-top but Abba just told me he doesn't like it. It's your own taste. Slice and enjoy!

recipes.summary: Ema normally makes this parve and gluten free, but it can also be made with dairy and non-gf ingredients.

recipes.title: Ema's Sweet Potato Pie-Kugel-Bake-Thing

items.text: Ema first made this for the Family Shabbos on 2/11/17. It was epic.
Ema forgot to write down the recipe as she was making it up, so these amounts are rough guess-timations.
As of yet, Ema has not made this for Thanksgiving, but I hereby declare that we shall make this for every Thanksgiving moving forward.
You can make this gluten free or not gluten free, and you can make this parve or dairy.
Large mixing bowl - for mixing filling
Small mixing bowl - for mixing topping
3/4 package of gluten free Kinnikinnick graham style crumbs (OR 10 1/2 ounces of any graham cracker crumbs) - reserve the last 1/4 of the crumbs in the box for the topping ingredients
6 tablespoons parve Smart Balance margarine OR butter, melted
1 large can of plain, mashed sweet potatoes (not sweet potato pie filling)
1/2 can of apple pie filling, crushed
2 T of corn syrup OR honey OR 1 T of molasses (for some depth)
1/2 cup of rice flour OR any type of flour
1/4 package of gluten free Kinnikinnick graham style crumbs (whatever is left over from the package)
3 T of Smart Balance margarine OR butter

To make the crust, take 3/4 package of graham cracker crumbs (keep the last 1/4 for the topping), add 1/4 cup granulated sugar and 6 tablespoons melted Smart Balance margarine. Mix and push it well into a round 9 inch pan and about an inch or two high on the sides. Refrigerate for an hour.

While the crust it is being chilled, combine in a large mixing bowl: 1 large can of cooked sweet potatoes, 1/2 can of crushed apple pie filling, 1/4 cup of sugar, 2 T of corn syrup or honey, 1 tsp of vanilla, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, a pinch of salt for flavor, 1/4 cup parve milk, and 1/2 cup of rice flour (or any type of flour). Mix well then add two eggs that have already been beaten. Blend everything well.
Take the chilled crust out of the refrigerator and pour the filling into it.
In a small bowl, mix 1/4 package graham cracker crumbs with 1/4 cup brown sugar and 3 T of smart balance margarine until you get coarse crumbs. Sprinkle over the top of the sweet potato mixture.
Put in the oven and bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until firm.

recipes.title: Savta's Favorite Cheese Blintzes

items.text: "Recipe adjusted for Israel....since I have no idea what cheese I have here."

"My mother Z"L used to make blintzes for lunchtime when I came home from school. Since I lived across the street from P.S.4 on Broome St. NYC (I spent from kindergarten to 6th grade there), it was easy for me to return home for a kosher homemade lunch, and some encouraging words from my mother. Roll and fry on the side where the wrap is closed. Then fry on both sides.

recipes.title: Ema's Moroccan Pashtida (potato kugel-type-thing)

items.text: You can choose to use 4 tablespoons of mayonnaise OR 1 teaspoon of onion powder + 2 tablespoons of honey +1 tablespoon of white vinegar
Wide pan - to cool the potatoes and mix the stuff
Frying pan with at least 3 inches of sides on it
6 medium Yukon Gold potatoes (if they're smaller or larger compensate accordingly)
1 tsp dried parsley flakes OR 3 T fresh chopped parsley
Optional: 2-3 cubes of defrosted frozen sautéed onions
Optional: 1 cup of canned peas and carrots
Optional: In some Moroccan homes, they like to add about 1 cup of cubed chicken or sweetbreads to the mixture before it is cooked (Ema doesn't normally do this)
Olive oil, coconut oil (expeller pressed isn't smelly) or palm oil
Fill a large pot with water and boil the potatoes. Potatoes should be covered very well in water.
Test the potatoes after 20 minutes and keep testing every 10 minutes to see if the potatoes are very soft.
When ready, drain and put in a wide pan to cool.
Peel the potatoes - but don't stress when some of it doesn't come off, it will just blend in.
Mash well. If there are some little chunks that's fine too.

Add 1 teaspoon of salt, 1/2 tsp of turmeric, a teaspoon of garlic powder and a teaspoon of parsley flakes. Then add EITHER 4 tablespoons of mayonnaise OR 1 teaspoon of onion powder + 2 tablespoons of honey + 1 tablespoon of white vinegar.

Mix well then add 1/4 cup of matzo meal (or any gluten-free 'Meal'), along with 1/2 teaspoon of baking powder, and 1 teaspoon of lemon juice, preferably fresh. Mix again then add 5 eggs one at a time, mixing well after each one.

Heat about 1/4 cup of oil in a pan with at least 3 inches of sides on it. When the oil is sizzling (I tested with a little bit of potato mixture) dump the whole potato mixture in and even out the top. Cover and cook over medium-low until the bottom and edges are firm, about 10 minutes (I check by putting a fork on the bottom and seeing if it got brown).

Dangerous: Very carefully, flip the hot pan over on a large plate, allowing the extra oil to drip into the sink. (I often do this with potholders but be careful that the oil does not get onto the potholders and burn you Chas vshalom.)

Now, add another two or 3 tablespoons of oil to the pan and heat until sizzling again. It takes maybe a minute or two because the pan is still hot. Slip the pashtida into the pan again, without covering and cook over medium heat until the bottom is brown. It should take about 5-10 minutes more. You do have to check it all the time though.
When the bottom is also brown, flip the pashtida over again onto a plate, again being careful that the oil does not burn you.
Decorate with mint or with lemon and serve warm (I decorated with lemon wedges and cilantro).

recipes.title: Ema's Meatballs in Sauce (Non-Tomato)

items.text: 3 squares of frozen sautéed onions, defrosted (or 1 sautéed onion)
3 slices of challah bread (Ema uses gluten-free Katz's)
In a Dutch oven add sauce ingredient, except for bay leaves, potato starch and 1 T water Start to cook on medium high while making the meat mixture.
Combine the meat ingredients and mix well using gloved hands.
Form into golf ball size balls and add to the sauce you started before in the pot. Cook on one side for a few minutes and then flip each meatball so that the other side gets cooked somewhat.
Now, gently add 4 cups of hot water along the edge of the pot, so that the meatballs do not crumble. Add 2 bay leaves.
Cook on medium high for 10 minutes uncovered then lower heat to medium low for 30 more minutes, Stirring occasionally.

In a small bowl take 1 tablespoon of potato starch and 1 tablespoon of water. Mix until not clumpy then add another quarter cup of cold water. Add to the meatballs in the pan. Gently mix. Cook until sauce has thickened. Remove bay leaves.
Remove from fire and serve over yellow oily spaghetti along with a lettuce salad, using Romain lettuce, fresh lemon juice, salt and olive oil.

recipes.title: Ema's Salted Caramel & Chocolate Hazelnut Popcorn

items.text: This can be made dairy or parve.
¾ cup light brown sugar. (I didn't have light brown sugar so I used dark brown sugar - take that!)
½ cup unsalted butter (I used Wayfare pareve butter)
½ tbsp. kosher salt * (I did not use this because the pareve butter that I used had salt already)
¾ cup hazelnut-chocolate spread (I used parve hazelnut chocolate spread)
Preheat oven to 250º. Line 2 rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper.

Combine brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, salt, vanilla and baking soda in a medium saucepan. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture is boiling and thickens slightly, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from heat, and whisk in hazelnut-chocolate spread.

Place popcorn in a very large bowl. Gradually add caramel mixture, stirring gently, until popcorn is evenly coated. Note: The bowl that I used was large but it was not large enough so I had to take in an enormous pot and mix it in that pot.

Spread popcorn evenly on prepared baking sheets. Bake in preheated oven, stirring occasionally, until mixture begins to harden, 20 to 30 minutes. Remove from oven, and let stand until hardened and crisp, 5 to 10 minutes.

recipes.summary: This can be made dairy or parve.

recipes.title: Franks and potatoes

items.text: Ema made this dish for the first time because Abba likes the way Evergreen makes it. What a treat.
2 packages cocktail franks (8 ounces each) OR 16 ounces of cut up frankfurters
6 large Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into chunks
Optional- Serve with sautéed different colored peppers, sliced and cooked with a little salt, garlic powder and honey
Cut the potatoes into chunks. Add them to a Dutch oven along with the spices.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes then add the can of diced tomatoes and 3 cubes of sautéed onions.
Bring to a boil and then add the cocktail franks.
Cover and cook for about 40 minutes over low heat, until the potatoes are soft but not mushy, .
Add water as necessary to make sure that it does not burn, but do not add too much because it will be wet rather than saucy.
When finished cooking through, most of the water should be gone and there should be a thick sauce at the bottom. Add salt to taste.
Serve with sautéed multi-colored peppers, sliced and cooked with a little salt, garlic powder and honey.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Hamatashen for Purim

Also, the link above has a different recipe that came out good also and I need to add in the recipe here
1 cup (2 sticks) of smart balance margarine, softened to room temperature

Beat margarine and sugar on high for 2-3 minutes. Add eggs in, one at a time.
In a separate bowl whisk the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and 3 cups of gluten free flour (leave out 1/4 cup).
Turn the mixer onto the lowest speed and add it to the wet mixture, 1/2 cup at a time. The dough should be soft but not sticky.
Divide the dough into 4 parts, roll each into a ball, wrap separately in plastic wrap and refrigerate for an hour.

Dust the counter and the rolling pin with flour. Remove 1 dough ball from the refrigerator, roll out, and cut into circles using 4 oz. mason jar or small juice glass (if the dough is too sticky to roll out and cut, add a tablespoon or more of flour).

recipes.title: Stuffed & Baked Flounder

items.text: This can be made dairy or parve.
Fresh or frozen flounder (Ema used frozen and defrosted it for an hour), 8-10 pieces
1/2 cup of breadcrumbs (Ema used gluten free) + more for topping fish
1/4 cup of either sour cream, mayonnaise or pareve ranch dip (which Ema used, the wayfare brand)
1 tsp salt + more for topping fish
1/2 tsp garlic powder + more for topping fish
1/4 tsp paprika + more for topping fish
1 T of honey (Ema only had date syrup so she used that)
If using frozen flounder, defrost it by leaving it out for an hour.
Take one bag of frozen broccoli florets and bake them in the oven for 40 minutes until soft (the bag that Ema used was 24 ounces but you really only need about 16 ounces for this.)
While that is baking prepare the food processor with the blade that you see in the picture.
When the broccoli is done baking, process it in the food processor with the frozen sautéed onions and the mushrooms.
When those are processed, add corn and 1/2 cup breadcrumbs. Process, more.
Then add 1/4 cup of either sour cream (it will be dairy), mayonnaise, or pareve ranch dip.
Mix that and then add 1 tsp of salt, 1/2 tsp of garlic powder, 1/4 tsp of turmeric and paprika, a 1/2 tsp of dried parsley flakes and 1 T of honey. Mix well.
Spay a cookie sheet with cooking spray and lay the flounder (defrosted if applicable) onto the pan.
Form the mixture into small balls and place onto the pieces of flounder. Roll up the pieces of flounder over the mixture.
Sprinkle some salt, garlic powder and paprika got over the tops of the flounder. If you have Panko crumbs then sprinkle them over that (if not you could just use breadcrumbs).
Spray the fish with cooking spray. Sprinkle a little bit more salt and a little bit more paprika over that (but not too much, just to give it color.)
Put in a preheated 350° oven for about 40 minutes or until crunchy on top.

recipes.title: Boiled Desert Artichokes

items.text: Bring a very large pot to a boil. Add salt and lemon halves.
Wash artichokes. Cut off the bottom stem and about a half inch from the top (as per picture.)
Cook over medium-high heat for about 45 minutes or until a "leaf" is soft.
Eat the leaves by biting out the mushy ends out with your teeth. When you're finished eating the leaves, cut off the bottom "heart" and eat it.
Some people dip the leaves and heart in a sauce made of mayonnaise and mustard.

recipes.title: Fluffy Cheesecake

items.text: This can be made parve and gluten free
You will need to refrigerate the cheesecake overnight before cutting into it, so plan ahead.
1 box (10 1/2 ounces) of grain cracker crumbs (Ema used Kinnikinnick gluten free)
6 tablespoons melted butter (Ema used Wayfair parve butter)
5 (8-ounce) blocks cream cheese at room temperature (Ema used Wayfare parve cream cheese)
1 pint sour cream, low-fat is fine (Ema used Wayfair parve sour cream)
2 lemons, juiced and with the rinds grated for lemon zest
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Grease a 10-inch springform pan.

Mix all of the crust ingredients together and push into the bottom of a 10 inch springform pan or 2 large aluminum Bundt pans (Ema used this). Refrigerate for an hour. (I have no patience to wait, so I put it into the freezer for a half hour)

Fill a roasting pan 1/4 full with hot water. Place your springform pan in the water bath and wait 10 minutes to see if any water seeps into your springform. (If so, dry it, grease it and place your springform in a pie dish. Then place the pie dish with the springform in the water bath.). Because I used the Bundt pans, I didn't have to do this part. Just be really careful because I ended up getting water into the pans.

In a large mixing bowl, add one block of cream cheese and beat it until creamy. Continue adding one block of cream cheese at a time and beating well. There must not be any lumps in your batter. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing after each addition on low. Add the remaining ingredients one at a time, mixing to combine after each addition. (OK let's be honest here, I just dumped everything in pretty much and let the food processor do its work.) Don't forget to add the juice of the lemons and the lemon zest. When all ingredients have been added, beat on high (or as high as you can without splashing) for seven minutes.

***Be really careful here when you put the filter pans into the water bath. Like I said above I got water in my pans so take it easy.***. Transfer the batter to the springform pan (filling it no more than 3/4 of the way to the top; see notes) in the water bath and bake for 10 minutes at 400 degrees F. Then lower the temperature to 375 degrees F and bake for 50-55 minutes. The top should be set, except for a small circle in the middle. Do not insert anything into the cheesecake to test it, or it will crack. Turn off the heat and let the cheesecake stay in the oven with the door ajar for one hour.

Remove the cheesecake and let it finish cooling on a wire rack. Refrigerate the cheesecake overnight before cutting into it. Store it in the refrigerator for up to three days or freeze it for up to 3 weeks.

Notes: If you only have a 9-inch springform pan, fill it 3/4 full with the batter. Bake the remaining batter in two ramekins or another suitable baking dish, in a water bath. Update 6-11-16: Even with a 10-inch springform, do not fill your pan any higher than 3/4 full. Bake any extra batter in ramekins in a water bath.

recipes.title: Macaroni with Tuna and Peas

Boil a large pot of water with salt and 1 T of olive oil.

recipes.title: Roasted Duck Legs

items.text: 1/2 tsp salt (for sauce) + more for seasoning duck
1/2 tsp of garlic powder (for sauce) + more for seasoning duck
Pat the skin dry and season it with salt, pepper (Ema omitted this) and garlic powder.
Put the duck legs skin side UP on a roasting pan in the oven, cook uncovered for 90 minutes.
In the middle of those 90 minutes (around 45 minutes for those who have trouble with math LOL), we are going to season the duck legs like this:
In a small bowl, mix together 3/4–1 cup of mango sauce, 2 tsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of rice vinegar (optional), 1/2 tsp of garlic powder, and 1/2 tsp of salt.

recipes.title: Seared Duck Breast

items.text: Duck breast (Ema uses breast that had already been taken off the bone - Pelleh is the company).
1/2 tsp salt (for sauce) + more for seasoning duck
1/2 tsp garlic powder (for sauce) + more for seasoning duck
1/2 cup Mango sauce, duck sauce or apricot jam
Season duck with salt, pepper (Ema omitted this),and garlic powder.
Cut the skin along the top about an inch every inch or so.
Put it in a cold pan then put the fire on medium to high heat - skin side DOWN. Cook it like that for 10 minutes while the fat drips off and the skin becomes golden brown. Flip the breast over.
Mix together mango sauce (or duck sauce or apricot jam), 1/2 tsp of garlic powder, 2 tsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tsp of salt. Spread it over the skin which is now on top and crunchy.
Cook for another 2 to 4 minutes. Serve with sliced oranges or mango and a sprig of mint if you have it.

recipes.summary: With duck breast, mango sauce & soy sauce.

recipes.title: Burekas with Potato Filling

items.text: 2 tsp of salt + more salting water and extra seasoning
Miniature puff party squares or large pastry squares (will need more filling)
Egg wash (beat 1 egg with 2 T of water)

Peel potatoes, then cut into small chunks, and drop into boiling water that has been well salted. Check them after 15 minutes to see if they are very soft inside. If they are not, keep checking them every five minutes with a fork. When done, drain the water then mash the potatoes.

Add sautéed onions, parve milk, mayonnaise, 2 teaspoons of salt, garlic powder, and turmeric. Mix well (the frozen onion should be defrosted by the hot potatoes). Taste to make sure there's enough salt. Ema always finds herself adding more because the potatoes “eat“ salt.
Defrost the puff pastry squares outside of the refrigerator until they get soft, about an hour or so. While defrosting, preheat the oven to 350°F and make the filling above.

To fill the puff pastry squares (the miniature ones) take for squares at a time, and put on a greased cookie sheet or plastic cutting board. On each square put about 1 to 2 t teaspoons of feeling. It should not take up that much room on the square. Now make the square into a triangle by folding one corner over to the other opposite corner. Press down along the open sides to seal well. Now take a fork and press down with it on those same edges. Continue this until all of the squares have been filled.
Put the squares on cookie sheets allowing enough space between each one for the increase in size when it bakes.

Now make egg wash (take an egg and mix it in a small bowl with a bit of water. This thins it out the egg enough to be able to spread it.) Take a food brush and spread the egg wash over the top of each of the burekas - doing not more than six at a time so that the egg wash does not dry out. After doing each six, sprinkle sesame seeds over the tops of those six. Now continue until you finished all of the burekas.
Put the cookie sheets in the oven and bake for about 40 minutes or until golden brown on top. Serve with mushroom sauce or just eat plain straight out of the oven.

items.text: 6 medium Yukon Gold potatoes - if they're smaller or larger compensate accordingly (It is very important that the potatoes are Yukon gold because they mash much more easily than the Idaho baking potatoes and Ema thinks they taste better. But – ‏אל טעם וריח אך אין מהלהתווכח - as they say, taste is in the mouth of the beholder.)
1 1/2 tsp of salt + more if needed
1/2 teaspoon of parsley flakes (or 1 T of fresh parsley)
4 T of mayonnaise OR 1 tsp of onion powder + 2 T of honey + 1 T of white vinegar
2-3 cubes of defrosted frozen sautéed onions

METHOD NUMBER ONE: Boil potatoes in enough water to cover well. Test after 20 minutes and keep testing every 10 minutes to see if they are very soft. When ready, drain and put in a wide pan to cool.peel, but don't stress when some of it doesn't come off - it will just blend in. Mash well.

METHOD NUMBER TWO: Peel potatoes then cut into small chunks and drop into boiling water that has been well salted. Check them after 15 minutes to see if they are very soft inside. If they are not, keep checking them every five minutes with a fork. When done, drain the water then mash the potatoes.

recipes.title: Moroccan Carrot Salad

Part of the Shabbat salad spread.

recipes.title: Chicken with Zucchini

items.text: This is one of Ema's famous "chicken with -" dishes
4 whole chicken legs (including the drumstick and thigh)
2 tablespoons of olive oil or coconut oil

Take chicken and put them in a Dutch oven over medium high heat. Heat for a few minutes and then turn over and heat for another 2 to 3 minutes. You can put 2 tablespoons of olive oil in but you don't have to. Just keep an eye on it if you don't.
Cover with 3-4 cups of water and bring to a boil then reduce heat to medium and cook for five minutes more.
While that is cooking, peel and cut potatoes into chunks, and cut zucchinis into 1 inch slices. Add to the pot.
Bing the chicken to the top using tongs or forks because that's already been partially cooked and you want the vegetables to get the spices in them also.

Reduce heat to low and partially cover. Cook for about a half hour to 40 minutes. Towards the end, keep an eye on the amount of liquid in the pot. You don't want to let it burn and, you also want to have enough liquid to make a ‏מבול but you don't want to make it to watery. If you find that there is too much liquid, take off the cover and let it cook on medium until the liquid becomes thicker. BUT YOU must watch it.

recipes.title: Shakshouka

items.text: Serves 2 to 4 depending upon how many eggs you give each person
7 or 8 soft diced tomatoes OR 1 large can + 1 small can of diced tomatoes (lately Ema's been doing that because it saves time)
1 one large red pepper, cut into small pieces but not diced
2 large or 3 small Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced
2 tsp salt + more for extra seasoning
Take a Dutch oven, add oil, and heat it on medium.
Add tomatoes, pepper, potatoes and spices.

Mix it all together and continue cooking, covered for 20 to 25 minutes or until the potatoes are soft. During that time pay attention to the water and make sure that it has not dried up. If you find that the water has dried up, add another cup and mix together.

Now, add eggs by cracking them gently, checking for blood spots and then putting on top of the mixture without mixing. You can sprinkle some salt on top now or later. Cover again and cook until the eggs are done to your liking. If you like them hard, Cook longer. (PS after putting the eggs in, Ema cooked it covered for another 10 minutes and the eggs were hard boiled. If somebody wants them soft boiled, they would put them in covered for five minutes approximately.)

recipes.title: Chicken Jerky for Star Wars Enthusiasts

items.text: Oh my glob this is exciting. A bunch of us yiddin eatin' jerky. I'm just thrilled.
Dehydrator preferred, otherwise use an oven. Go online and figure that part out yourself.
Ingredients are measured roughly. If you need someone to hold your hand and give you precise measurements, then you need to man up and figure it out, soldier!
Tenderize chicken breasts. Make sure to beat your meat very hard, it adds to the jerky flavor.
Throw chicken breasts into freezer for 15 min...makes them easier to cut.
Cut into long thin slices (the thinner they are the quicker they will dehydrate).

Prepare marinade.... I just kind of winged mine. It was a lot of teriyaki sauce, a good amount of worcestershire sauce, a bit of liquid smoke, a couple tablespoons of minced garlic, onion powder and schawarma seasoning.

1/8 cup of honey (if you don't want it very sweet you can reduce the sugar and or the honey)

recipes.title: A Guide to Choosing Fish for Shabbat Dagim

items.text: These are the normal fish that I (Ema) make on Shabbat:
Flounder, fillet - This often gets broken up into pieces so if you get the thicker pieces they're better. Also don't cook this as much as other pieces.
Turbo, fillet - This is cheaper than Seabass but tastes just like it. Very fatty fish.
Seabass, has bones - See above, expensive.
Nile perch, fillet - I don't like it so much but some people do.
Baby salmon, fillet - It has to be fresh and small. If it's too big it just doesn't come out as good.

Whitefish, has bones - Do not get it deboned because the bones actually give it a really good flavor when it cooks. This is our favorite fish of all. It has a lot of bones and they're very small so you have to be careful eating it.

Tile, has bones - This was our favorite fish when we first got married. You can only find it at certain fish places but if you find it it's really delicious. Again, do not filet it but rather cook it with its bones because they give it really good flavor. The bones are much larger than whitefish. This can be somewhat expensive but it's definitely worth it, in my opinion.

Carp, has bones - We don't usually buy carp in America because it can taste like dirt. In Israel though, the Carpiyon is raised in lakes and is very small compared to the American carp and much much tastier. It also has tiny little bones so you have to be careful.
Please note: we absolutely hate, HATE, tilapia! It tastes like dirt no question.

Many people use red snapper, sole, halibut, and even trout. I haven't found them to be very tasty but it's a matter of taste so you can try it and see. In Israel, Doda Sara uses something called Baccala which is some sort of dried salted fish. I'm not 100% what it's made out of but if anybody else knows please tell me.

recipes.summary: Flounder, fillet - This often gets broken up into pieces so if you get the thicker pieces they're better.

recipes.title: Ktsisot Dagim - Moroccan Fish Balls for Shabbat

items.text: Ema estimated the amounts she used, some might not be 100% accurate.

2 T to 1/4 cup olive oil, preferably Geffen mild (in real Moroccan fish they use about a cup of olive oil or more. If you're trying to save calories use less but if you want it to really taste good put as much in as you can).
2 1/2 pounds of ground Pike and whitefish (no sugar)
To a large Dutch oven with high sides, add the sauce ingredients (minus the carrots and peppers.)
Heat on high until it starts to boil, then lower heat to medium low.
Mix the fish ingredients together in a large mixing bowl.

recipes.title: M'gena - Moroccan Egg and Chicken Loaf

items.text: The actual name is La Maguina.
Abba goes cray for this. It's real good.

You can use fresh pees and carrots if you want, but the canned stuff makes the job quicker. If using fresh carrots, dice one, and stir fry in olive oil for 5 minutes until brown. When it's done add the onions and peppers and cook.
1/2 red bell pepper, seeded and diced
1 can of pees and carrots, drained
3 T bread crumbs (Ema uses gluten free)
Cooking spray or something to grease a pan
Generously oil a nonstick loaf pan.
In a large skillet heat 3 T of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the red pepper and onions, cook until lightly browned, for 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, bread crumbs, and spices until frothy. Add the rest of ingredients and mix.

recipes.title: Meat Burekas

items.text: Ema doesn't always make Meat Burekas, but when she does...oowa, owwa.
One package of frozen puff pastry (about 12 squares)
1 tsp cumin (more if you like cumin ）
Optional: two or three squares of frozen sautéed onions
Cooking spray or something to grease a baking sheet

Remove the puff pastry dough from the freezer. Open up the package and try to gently pry each piece then put it onto a plastic cutting board or silver foil. This will allow it to defrost all at the same time.
Dump the chopped meat into a large frying pan. Take a large fork and crush the chop meat as it is cooking over a medium flame. When the chopped meat looks like it is crushed, drain the juices.
Then add in all of the spices and the honey (and the squares of sautéed onions if you're using them).

Heat over a medium flame until the chopped meat is not red anymore. (In order to bind the meat, you could also add a beaten egg - after you take the meat off the fire and cool it down. I didn't do that because it just takes too long.)
Remove the chop meat from the fire and let cool.
Separate the pastry squares from each other.

When cool, or at least not too hot, put a heaping tablespoon of the meat onto one corner of each puff pastry square. Fold the opposite side over on top of the meat, then put a little bit of water on the bottom two sides and seal the top to the bottom. (OK, I'm too lazy to put the water on and I just seal the sides without the water but it doesn't work all the time.)
Using a fork, push down along the two edges that you just sealed so that you have nice edges.
Gently take each Bureka and place on a greased cookie sheet leaving a little space between each one so that it can rise.

Now mix the beaten egg with a tablespoon of water and using a food brush, spread that and water mixture over each bureka. Don't do more than three at a time. Now sprinkle sesame seeds over the egg wash. Repeat until all of the Burekas have been coated.
Put in a preheated 350° oven for 40 or 50 minutes, until golden on top. Remove and try not to eat them all up. :-)

recipes.title: Zucchini Kugel

items.text: Zucchini is a vegetable that is filled with water so the ingredients, especially the matzo meal or round crackers, are approximate.
