Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat 2 oblong pans with olive oil.

Using a food processor with the grinder attachment (see picture), process half of the zucchini then dump it out into a bowl and process the other half. This makes it easier to grind. (If you are using carrots, then put half into 1 grinding bunch and half into the other.)

Using a large strainer, dump the zucchini (or zucchini/carrot) mixture in. Take a large spoon or fork and press down on the zucchini mixture to remove as much moisture as possible. Some people also use paper towels on top of the mixture to absorb the moisture.
When you've gotten as much moisture out as possible, dump everything into a very large bowl. Add in the salt, garlic powder, turmeric, defrosted onions, honey and matzo meal.

Now is a good time to taste to make sure that there's not too little or too much salt. Add salt as needed but carefully. It is also a good time to check the moisture level and see if it is still wet. If you feel that it is still too moist, add another quarter for half cup of matzo meal or ground crackers.
Now add the beaten eggs and mix well. Pour half of the mixture into one oblong pan and half into the other then bake at 350° for approximately 50 minutes – one hour, or until golden brown on top.

items.text: Savta: "Kashe Varnishkes were a staple in our house. My mother made it as a side dish with meat at least once a week. Generally it was made for Shabbat, since it entailed three different pots."
Read through the instructions before you make this dish. you can do steps 1 to 3 simultaneously, or separately, depending on how coordinated you are and how many pans you want to use at once.
1 or 2 large frying pans for onions and kasha (you can cook them simultaneously by using two pans, or one after the other by using the same pan)
1 box of Kasha (buckwheat kernels) - not sure on how much Savta actually uses, this is an estimate, I need to update this.
Prepare bowtie pasta according to box directions. Drain and put aside.
Fry 3 large chopped onions until golden brown. Set aside

Start to boil a pot of water for the kasha. Place kasha in a frying pan with oil and frying until kernels begin to open then mix a scrambled egg into it. (Savta: "I think that the egg makes the kernels appear larger and adds to the taste. My mother usually added an egg, though you do not have to.") After they are browned, pour boiling water over kasha and cook according to box directions.

When all three steps are completed, in a large mixing bowl combine the pasta, onions an kasha until they are well mixed, careful not to break the bowties. My mom added Shmaltz, which, of course, we no longer use.
Add salt to taste and enjoy.

recipes.summary: Savta: "Kashe Varnishkes were a staple in our house.

recipes.title: Savta's Creamed Mushrooms

items.text: 3 T fried onions (you can use the frozen stuff, just defrost it)
2 heaping T of sour cream (or substitute if Fleishig)
If you don't have fried onion, sauté a chopped onion now.
Peel mushrooms and cut into pieces.
Place in large frying pan and fry for about 3 minutes on high flame.
Add fried onions and mix with mushrooms.
Mix sour cream and flour with a little water and add to mushroom mixture.
Stir until thickened. If more flour is needed, add.
Serve on toasted bread or baked potato ....mmmmm good.

recipes.summary: With fried onions, fresh mushrooms, sour cream & flour.

recipes.title: Broccoli Kugel

items.text: You can make the same thing using chopped spinach. Remember that there is much more water in the chop spinach so you must drain it very well.
Strainer to remove excess broccoli water
Large mixing bowl to combine all ingredients
1/2 cup gluten free matzah meal OR regular matzah meal
1 tsp salt - add more to taste later on, before you add in eggs

Defrost broccoli and strain it. This is how Ema does it - To defrost broccoli, remove broccoli from bag, place into microwave safe bowl and microwave for about 8 minutes on high. When it's done, place broccoli into a strainer, and remove as much excess water as you can by pushing down on it with a fork.
Combine all ingredients, except for the eggs. Taste and add more salt if necessary.
Pour mixture into 2 small, greased, rectangular pans (the kugel cooks more consistently like this than in larger pans)

recipes.summary: With eggs, frozen chopped broccoli, defrosted sautéed onions & garlic powder.

recipes.title: Savta's Salad Dressing

items.text: There are two recipes, probably because it changes every times Savta makes it.
Savta is famous for this dressing. The amounts you should use is anyone's guess.
Recipe 2 - Orlee got this from Savta in May 2024

recipes.summary: There are two recipes, probably because it changes every times Savta makes it.

recipes.title: 5 Min. Southern Fried Chicken ala Sue Zeitlin Z'L

items.text: 2 heaping tablespoons of onion soup mix
Combine onion soup, organo and corn flake crumbs in plastic bag.
Roll chicken legs into combined mixture.
Bake for about 20 minutes in 400 degree oven.

recipes.summary: With chicken legs, onion soup mix, corn flake crumbs & organo.

recipes.title: Cheese Burekas

items.text: Small mixing bowl for egg wash
Pastry brush or something to brush on the egg wash with
1 package of puff pastry squares – Usually 12 in a package (you can use the package of 36 mini squares also but use less filling and less time in the oven)
1 package of feta cheese or 1/2 package of feta cheese and 1/2 package of Farmer cheese
Optional black pepper (about a half teaspoon)
1 egg, mixed with a tablespoon of water
Using Pam, lightly grease a cookie sheet. You might need 2.
Mix cheese with garlic powder, salt and pepper.

As per the potato and meat Burekas, put a heaping teaspoon of cheese filling into one corner of a puff pastry square. If you want to make the edges stick better, brush a little water over the two edges closest to the filling. Fold over the opposite corner on top of the corner with the cheese filling and push down along the edges that have been folded over, with your fingers. Now take a fork and push down over those same edges. Put the finished Burekas on the greased cookie sheet.

Using a pastry brush, dip the brush into the egg mixture and gently brush over the tops of all the Burekas, doing three at a time. Then dump sesame seeds over the tops of the Burekas that have been coated with the egg mixture.
When all are done, put the cookie sheets with the Burekas into the oven and bake for about 45 to 50 minutes or until golden brown on top.

recipes.summary: With puff pastry squares, feta cheese, garlic powder & topping.

recipes.title: Kalesha (Cornmeal) Made My Mother's Way

items.text: Savta ate this every day for lunch. Saba says it's a Galitzyana food and he never ate it until he met Savta.
1 tsp salt (will probably need more to taste)
Fill a medium sized pot with cold water.
Combine water, kalesha, salt and sugar in a medium sized pot. Mix.
Put flame on high and wait for mix to boil, mixing consistently. It bubbles up and pops so be careful !!!
Once boiled, lower flame to low and continue vigorously mixing about 7-8 minute until all the water is absorbed and the Kalesha is the consistency of oatmeal.
When done, pour into flat plate, make a hole in the middle with a tablespoon, and fill with cottage cheese topped with sour cream (my mother, Bubby Bertha used butter first).
If the corn meal does not have a sweet and salty taste, add sugar and or salt as needed.
Savta spreads out the cream cheese and sour cream all over the kalesha and Saba mixes it all together.

recipes.summary: Savta ate this every day for lunch.

recipes.title: Baked Ziti (Gluten Free)

items.text: One package of Tinkyada Penne pasta (16 ounces)
One container of Lactaid cottage cheese (16 ounces)
One jar of pasta sauce or marinara sauce (I use Barilla 24 ounces)
2 to 3 cups of mozzarella cheese, shredded (OK, I do put too much in so you can put less if you want to. I just like it really cheesy.)
1/2 teaspoon of dried parsley flakes, optional
Cook pasta as per directions on the package being careful to not over cook.
While the pasta is cooking, take a 9 x 13 lasagna pan and spray with Pam.
When pasta is finished cooking, drain and rinse with cold water.

In the same pot that you used to cook the pasta, put the cottage cheese along with the drained pasta. Add the spices and salt.Add the pasta sauce . Mix gently. Add half of the mozzarella cheese and mix again gently. Spread the other half of the mozzarella cheese over the mixture.
Dump the mixture into the sprayed 9 x 13 pan. Cover well with two pieces of foil that have been sprayed with Pam (in the middle only so that the pasta does not stick).

Cook at 350°F for 15 minutes. Remove the silver foil and cook at 400° for another 10 minutes so that the top of the big ziti is crunchy. If you don't like it crunchy then don't do the extra 10 minutes of cooking. That's my (Ema's) favorite part though!
Remove from oven and let sit for a few minutes because it's really hot then eat and enjoy.

recipes.summary: With tinkyada Penne pasta, lactaid cottage cheese, pasta sauce & mozzarella cheese.

recipes.title: Chanofsky Secret Sauce

items.text: 1/4 cup deli mustard plus one T
1/2 lime (when mixed, taste and see if you need a full one)
Mix all ingredients together. See if you need to add another 1/2 lime.
Refrigerate in a squeeze tube for easy pouring.
Eat with anything and everything. Great with artichokes. Ross squeezes it on his chicken and rice.

recipes.summary: With mayo, yellow mustard, paprika & lime.

recipes.title: Potato Pastellot (Moroccan Potato Pancakes)

items.text: A second version of the recipe was given on 10/2020.
The picture I have shows that the fire was on too high because the Pastellot got black instead of golden brown. Pay attention to the heat level. If it gets too hot, lower the heat.
If you feel that the they are too loose, add a tablespoon or two more of matzo meal, mix and then let sit for a minute or two before frying.
It's actually easier to make these a little bit smaller because they won't break when you flip them over.
To make with less oil, use a good nonstick frying pan and use cooking spray or very little oil. Pay attention so that it doesn't burn.
Large soup pot to cook potatoes
One and a half teaspoons of salt
2 tablespoons of mayonnaise (not original way to make it but tastes really creamy)
1/3 of a cup of matzo meal (of course I use gluten-free)
3 to 4 tablespoons of oil for frying
About six large Yukon Gold potatoes or the approximate amount of medium potatoes
Salt (Start with a teaspoon and then add more after to taste)
Smart balance (or similar) margarine (About one large tablespoon)
1/2 to 1 cup of matzo meal (i used gluten-free) depending upon how loose the mixture is
In a large pot filled with water cook the Yukon Gold potatoes until they are soft when a fork is pushed into them.
In a large bowl or pot with a flatbottom mash the Yukon Gold potatoes. You can peel them if you like or leave the skins on for more vitamins.

Add all of the other ingredients except the matzo meal and eggs. Taste and then add more salt if necessary. (You don't need too much salt but if you don't have enough they will be very bland). They should taste a little bit saltier than you would like for mashed potatoes. After you add the eggs and matzo meal the salt levels off.
Add matzo meal then add eggs and mix well. Let sit for a few minutes to let the matzo meal get absorbed.
While waiting, heat oil in a large frying pan until it sizzles when a drop of water is put in.
Drop tablespoon size mounds of mixture into the hot oil.

Gently place into the frying pan being careful not to get burned by the hot oil. Fry until the bottom is golden brown, then gently flip over and fry the other side until golden brown. (If you have no more oil left in the pan add a couple of more tablespoons).
Drain on paper towels and serve hot and crispy.
Preheat oven to 350°F. (You could even put it up to 375 if you want to go more quickly.)
Boil potatoes (peeled or unpeeled) until soft usually about 20 to 30 minutes. (If unpeeled, make sure there are no hard stems or black spots and if there are, remove them.)
Add salt, garlic powder, onion powder, turmeric, mayonnaise and Margarine to taste. Mix well and add the onions. (If the mixture is not hot anymore, melt the onions in a microwave first then add.)
Add matzo meal until thick. Let’s set a couple of minutes then add eggs. Mix well.
Onto a cookie sheet sprayed with Pam, Form mixture into patties then place on cookie sheet with a little space between them.
** Bake in oven for about 45 to 55 minutes depending upon how crispy you want the tops. Eat warm
** Please note: You can form the mixture into patties and then fry in hot oil. Yes I know, it’s not healthy but it’s so so good LOL.

recipes.summary: The picture I have shows that the fire was on too high because the Pastellot got black instead of golden brown.

recipes.title: Chicken with Swiss Chard (Chicken with Green Stuff)

items.text: Ema made this for only two people. If you want to make it for more people, be gentle when adding more spices. You might want to taste it later on and then add Salt and spices to taste.
2 chicken legs (thigh and drum stick together), defrosted
A tablespoon or two of honey
2 bunches of Swiss chard, washed well and cut into medium pieces

Put about a half inch of water into a Dutch oven pot. Add spices and bring to a boil then add in the two chicken legs. Drizzle a little bit of honey on top to take away the bitterness of the Swiss chard.

Cook until chicken looks like it's done on the outside. It does not have to be cooked on the inside yet. Add the tomato sauce (if it looks like the water has evaporated, add a can of water) and mix well. Bring to a boil and add the Swiss chard, cut into pieces as per picture. (It is going to look like there's too much with chard. As you cover it and heat it up, the amount will decrease by about half. It is easier to mix it at that point).

Bring to a boil and lower fire to medium low, cover and cook until chicken is cooked through (on the inside) approximately 45 to 55 minutes. You might have to add more water so check it in the middle to make sure it did not dry up. Serve immediately.

recipes.summary: Ema made this for only two people.

recipes.title: Sweet Noodle Kugel

items.text: Makes a medium kugel not large. For a larger one double The recipe and use a 9 x 13 pan but do NOT double vanilla
One 12 ounce package medium egg noodles
Salt for the water for the egg noodles
3 tablespoons of honey (You can leave it out if you don't want it to sweet)
One can of apple pie filling (if you don't like chunky, you can take A fork and mush it before putting it in)

Note: I used to make this with fruit cocktail (canned) instead of The apple pie filling. Some people prefer it but if you do this, you need to add some sugar (maybe a quarter of a cup )and a thickening agent Like matzo meal, 1/4–1/2 cup.
1/2 cup of pareve milk or pareve whipping cream
Cook egg noodles as per directions on package (and salt the water) but take it out a minute before hand and drain with cold water in a colander.
Add rest of ingredients except eggs. Mix then add eggs. Mix well and pour into the greased pan. Cook at 350°F for approximately 50 minutes – one hour or until the top is golden. Serve warm.

recipes.summary: Makes a medium kugel not large.

recipes.title: Alex's Baked Garlic Sesame Cod

items.text: This is a no fail recipe. Its easy, yummy, quick and healthy. Great for a weeknight dinner. Sorry its not super exact, didn't know it was gonna be so good until we made it. Next time we make this I will post exact measurements. Oh and I ate this with rice. The sauce is yummy with it - Orlee
This recipe is enough for 2 people
1-1.5 lbs of fresh (not frozen) cod fillets, no skin
Asian Mehn Sesame Garlic Sauce - you can get this in any supermarket. Or at least the kosher ones carry it.
On a silver foil sheet, spray it with Pam, then place cod fish on top.
Season with moderate amount of salt, heavy on the pepper, moderate garlic powder, and lastly 1/4-1/2 cup of the Sesame Garlic Sauce.
Alex let his fish sit for about 30 minutes. Orlee is not that patient.

Now you need to make a basket out of silver foil, leaving enough to wrap it closed. So basically layer three sheets of silver foil, then place the one with the fish in the center of it and wrap it shut. If you are talented enough to do this with two sheets, thats great but you may end up with fish sauce all over your oven. Are you willing to risk that?
I swear its godly. Its game of thrones yummy. Its better than the big turkey legs people eat at amusement parks.
May the force be with you.

recipes.summary: This recipe is enough for 2 people

recipes.title: Salad Matbucha: (Moroccan tomato and pepper salad, cooked)

items.text: One red and one green pepper OR six baby peppers
I handful of fresh parsley, chopped
1 1/2 teaspoons (Sweet) Paprika (You can use a half teaspoon of spicy Paprika if you want it a little bit spicy)
1/2 teaspoon each of cayenne (red ) and black pepper, optional (it will be spicy)
1 to 2 long hot spicy peppers, very optional (If you use these spicy peppers, it might be better to omit the spicy Paprika , and the red pepper)
1/4 cup of oil, optional for those who don't want it to be caloric but important if you don't car

Take core out of tomatoes and coarsely chop. Some people take off the skin also but I don't feel it's worth the time and effort. Core and coarsely chop (all) peppers. Add them to the pan along with the parsley and spices. Add oil and water. Mix well and cook over medium low flame for approximately 45 minutes – one hour. During that time mix after every 15 minutes. If you notice that the water is drying up, add another quarter cup each time you see it dry. Then mix well again.
When it's ready, there should be no more water left and the peppers and tomatoes should be cooked well and mixed.
Eat with fresh bread or as a cracker/ chip dip.

recipes.summary: With tomatoes, garlic powder, tumeric & paprika.

recipes.title: Tongue in Tomato Sauce

items.text: If you have never made this before (which I doubt anyone but Ema has), just know that a whole raw tongue is terrifying. You've been warned.
One large tongue, pickled (if you can't find a pickled tongue, boil it with pickled spices and add extra spices. Throw away spices when done.)
One can (15 ounce) of plain tomato sauce
1 teaspoon of salt (After cooking the sauce taste it and then add more salt if necessary to taste)
Three cubes of sautéed onions, frozen
1 tablespoon of honey (I just drizzle it in and eyeball it)
1/4 cup of raisins, optional, but I make it this way

In a very large saucepan, put the Tongue (defrosted). Cover with water and make sure it is at least 2 inches above it. Boil. Lower heat to medium low. Let cook for one and a half to two hours. If the water evaporates below the tongue, add more to cover well.

Remove from heat and drain. Let cool but do not put in refrigerator. When it is cool enough to handle, peel off the fix skin around the top of the tongue using a knife if necessary. It should come off easily if it's been cooked enough.

Put about 3 inches of water into a sauce pan. Add the rest of the sauce ingredients and bring to a boil. Lower heat to medium and boil them for about 10 minutes. Add the tongue and mix. Bring to the boil again and lower heat to medium and cook for about a half hour – 45 minutes.
Serve warm over rice (or couscous perhaps).

recipes.summary: If you have never made this before (which I doubt anyone but Ema has), just know that a whole raw tongue is terrifying.

recipes.title: Chicken with apricot jam recipe

Instead of the rice pilaf are use regular rice because I make a gluten-free. I don't use the raisins because Ilan doesn't like raisins."

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Quiche (Crustless): A light sweet treat

items.text: Anytime Ema makes a cheese quiche I plotz.
16 ounces (1 pound) cottage cheese, I used Lactaid
2 tablespoons sour cream, I used Lactaid
2 tablespoons of sugar (you can use sweet and low or Stevia)
4 tablespoons Matzo meal or cake meal (of course I used gluten free)
One full cup of sour cream (again I used Lactaid)
2 1/2 tablespoons of sugar or and equal amount of the sweeter of your choice
Grease a 8 x 8 pan or two small pans as per picture.
Mix everything except eggs then taste. Make sure it's sweet enough for you and if not add some more sweetener (sugar, Stevia or honey). But add only one teaspoon at a time then taste again.
When it is sweet enough for your taste, add the eggs.
Mix until fully blended. Pour into greased pan(s). If using two pans they will be done quicker than if using the one pan, so pay attention.

Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes. (For small pans and 35 minutes for large pan). Spread topping over quiche. Bake for another 15 -25 minutes or until slightly golden. It actually took me another 25 minutes to get the top looking golden.
Bake at 350°F for 35 to 45 minutes until golden on top.
After shutting the oven, you can keep the door open and leave the quiche there for another 20 minutes, or gently put it on top of the hot oven and leave it there so that it won't implode.
Cut and serve warm. You can add a topping like cherry or apple pie filling if you want it really sweet. Otherwise use fresh strawberries, raspberries or blueberries.

recipes.summary: Anytime Ema makes a cheese quiche I plotz.

recipes.title: Sweetbreads in Rotev (sauce)

items.text: 3 to 4 packages of sweetbreads (I always make this with 3 to 4 packages of sweetbreads because otherwise the work just doesn't make sense )
One pint container of pareve milk or almond milk if you are Leyat
One and a half teaspoons salt
One and a half teaspoons of dried parsley flakes
Two Enormous cans of mushrooms, drained (like the 28 ounce kind)
2 teaspoons of potato flour/potato starch, mixed with a few teaspoons of cold water in a cup or bowl until there are no more lumps.

Cook defrosted sweet breads in a very large pot with vinegar and water to cover plus more for about 1 1/2 hours. Remove from flame and carefully drain. Let cool. Put into A disposable pan. Throw out any leftover water in the pot.

Using a paring knife or a very sharp knife (not a large one), carefully scrape the skin off of the meat of the sweet breads. (The skin is kind of like a big sticky membrane). You won't be able to get everything off but get the big pieces of skin off. Gently break into smaller pieces.

Put the rest of the ingredients, except for the potato starch mixture, into the pot that you just used (so that you don't have to wash another pot). Cook over medium flame until boiling and then immediately lower the flame to simmer. Add the sweetbreads that have been skinned and broken into smaller pieces. Bring to a boil again over a medium flame and then bring it back down to a simmer. After about 10minutes that it has been simmering, add the potato starch and mix well. Simmer for another 10 minutes.
MUST serve over potato or meat Burekas.

photos.caption: This is how you clean sweatbreads
Sticky, stringy things are the skin/membranes
What the sweetbreads should look like when they are de-skinned

recipes.summary: With sweetbreads, vinegar, pareve milk & garlic powder.

recipes.title: Ema's Chicken Soup (Moroccan)

items.text: Abba is VERY specific about how he likes his chicken soup, and Ema got the formula down to a T. No butternut squash, yes to sweet potatoes.
You can probably find a lot of these vegetables pre-chopped at the supermarket
1 large chicken cut up or 4 large chicken legs, defrosted
2 large sweet potatoes, cut into medium chunks OR 2 cups of cut up butternut squash (if you're not cooking for Abba)
One large handful of parsley, fresh, chopped
One large handful of cilantro, fresh, chopped
A few sprigs of fresh dill, chopped OR four squares of frozen chopped dill
2 teaspoons of salt (add more at the end to taste)
Three dried Bay leaves, to be removed before serving

Add water to a very large soup up to about 2/3 full. Over high heat on the stove, add chicken and bring to a boil. Lower heat to medium and boil for about 10 minutes. This gives the chicken time to cook inside without making the vegetables too mushy.
Add the rest of the ingredients. Mix and cover. (OK, I don't always cover my soup but I do add water when it evaporates).
Cook for about an hour or at least until the center of the chicken is not pink anymore and the vegetables are soft.
Optional: Remove chicken from soup into a pan and let cool. Take off skin and bones and pulled chicken into smaller pieces but not too small. Add chicken back to the soup pot.
You can serve with noodles or matzoh balls or rice or just with mini croutons (see picture).

recipes.summary: Abba is VERY specific about how he likes his chicken soup, and Ema got the formula down to a T.

recipes.title: French Roast

items.text: 3–5 cubes of sautéed onions, defrosted (Or one Spanish onion diced, sautéed with 2 tablespoons of oil)
One package (4 tablespoons) onion soup mix
One small jar of sweet and sour duck sauce
1 packet of onion soup mix (4 Tablespoons)
If using Spanish onion, heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet and sauté the onion and oil.

Smear onions over roast and sprinkle pepper (if using), garlic powder and paprika liberally. Put duck sauce and onion soup into a small bowl, mix together and pour over roast. You can change the ratio of duck sauce if you like it sweeter or with more sauce.
Marinate overnight or for a few hours. Cover tightly and bake covered 2-2 1/2 hours (To keep it softer I often bake for 3 hours) at 350°F. Uncover for 1/2 hour to brown the meat. Based often.
Before Cutting the meat, let cool. It taste really good when it’s reheated after being cut in its sauce.

Optional: to make gravy, remove the sauce and put into a small pot. Take about 4 tablespoons of potato starch and mix with cold water. Add to the sauce and stir continuously over medium heat until thickened.
Mix cranberry sauce and onion soup mix (or spices) together in a bowl.
Put the roast into the pan. Pour the sauce over the roast and mush into it.
Cook covered for 1/2 hours on 350. Lower heat to 280 degrees. Cook for another 3 1/2 hours.

Optional - After the roast is taken out of the oven, put all of the gravy into a sauce pan and add 2 tablespoons of potato flour or potato starch mixed with a quarter cup of water. Put the fire on medium under the gravy and mix until thickened. Then, pour back over the brisket which has been cut. It gives it a nice thick sauce.

These pictures begin after the roast has already been taken out of the oven. The first picture is the gravy without the potato starch. Next is the potato starch mixed with water then put back into the gravy thickened and poured over the cut roast.
Ema got this recipe from a woman in Wesley Kosher, who got it from the man behind the butcher counter. Clearly this recipe has real yichus.
You can make this with French Roast or with Bristket - second cut Brisket (not the first cut).
1 metal roasting pan OR Two 9x13 aluminum pans (Ema doubles up the pans to make them sturdier when cooking)

recipes.summary: With french roast, sautéed onions, garlic powder & paprika.

recipes.title: Savta's Latkes for Chanukah

items.text: You can use this recipe for latkes or kugel. I made a kugel, and tasted a few latkes to perfect the recipe
Wash and scrub potatoes. Do NOT peel.

Put potatoes and onion through a food processor The potatoes can either come out stringy, or if you use a blade in the processor that grates them then they will be a texture similar to normal kugels. Let set for a few minutes and drain the liquid.
Combine potatoes and onions with rest of ingredients (minus cooking spray).
Bake in 375 degree oven for about an hour (check after 45 mins.) I put mine into a convection oven at 400 degrees for about 1/2 hour.
As you can see from the picture, the kugel is white even though the potatoes weren't peeled. (Pics are still missing!).

recipes.summary: As promised, the "easy" Latke recipe

recipes.title: Simple Stuffing for Thanksgiving

items.text: 2 tablespoons of olive oil or coconut oil
1 pound of good day-old bread (I used gluten-free Challah)
One and a half cups chopped onions (mine happened to have been red)*
One a half cups 1/4 inch sliced celery *
One and a half cup of 1/4 inch sliced carrots *
2 tablespoons of fresh chopped dill or four squares of frozen dill
2 tablespoons of fresh chopped cilantro or four squares of frozen cilantro
2 squares of frozen fried onions, defrosted
1 teaspoon of freshly ground black pepper (Optional - I did not use this)
2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth divided (obviously if you use chicken broth, this will not be parve)
*I didn’t have to bother with that chopping. I just bought a container of each of these From Wesley Kosher already chopped. Drop the mic!
Spray a 13 x 9 cookie sheet with cooking spray and set aside.
Scatter bread in a single layer on a (different) big cookie sheet. Bake at 250°, stirring occasionally, until dried out about one hour. Let cool. Transfer to a very large bowl.
Meanwhile melt 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet over medium high heat; add onions and celery. Stir often until just beginning to brown about 10 minutes. Add to bowl with bread.
Put second tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet and add eggplant and carrots. Stir again until just getting brown and eggplant is very soft. Add this to bowl with bread also.
Stir in herbs, salt and pepper. Drizzle in 1 1/4 cup broth and toss gently. Let cool.

Whisk 1 1/4 cups broth and eggs in a small bowl. Add to bread mixture: fall gently until thoroughly combined. Transfer to prepared baking dish. Cover with foil and bake until an instant read thermometer inserted in the center of the dressing registers 160°F, about 40 minutes. (OK, I didn’t do this. I just baked it for about 50 minutes to make sure)
At this point, I cooled it uncovered and then covered it again and put it in the freezer. You don’t have to freeze it now just continue to the next step.
If it’s frozen,Take it out of the freezer, uncover it and bake it until the top is browned and crisp about 50 to 60 minutes longer.
If you did not freeze it, only bake it about 40 to 45 minutes. I find that the gluten-free bread might need to be baked a little extra in order to be crispy on top.

recipes.summary: With olive oil, good day-old bread, sliced celery & chopped flat leaf parsley.

recipes.title: Chicken with Onions, Prunes and Raisins

items.text: 1 large package of full chicken legs (Ema's had 5 in it)
4-6 onions, peeled and diced (Ema used two red onions here instead of two large Spanish onions because she didn't have the two large Spanish onions. It came out fine though.)
Put chicken in a large dutch oven with 2 cups of water on medium high heat.
Cook on each side for about five minutes until each side looks done on the outside.
Add everything else in, minus the onions.
Reduce heat to medium low and cover. Cook for 15 minutes.
During that time peel the onions and cut into pieces like in the pics.
After 15 minutes, put those into the pot.
Add another 1 to 2 cups of water depending upon how wide the pan is (the wider the pan, the more water you need because it evaporates more quickly).
Mix the whole pan well leaving the chicken on top so that the onions can cook. Cover again and cook on medium low for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Open the pan and if there is still a lot of water left, Cook for another 10 or 15 minutes until the water becomes thicker but not until the water evaporates. Remember, you need your sauce.
Eating directions: Serve with lettuce salad and lemon. Also, you can serve with toasted rolls like Udi's gluten free rolls in the picture.

recipes.summary: With full chicken legs, paprika, cumin & cinnamon.

recipes.title: Orlee's Vegan Broccoli Salad

items.text: This is a vegan and gluten-free yummy nosh salad. Contains cashew nuts (which means it has tannons!)
2 large broccoli crowns (florets only), finely chopped
⅓ cup roasted salted almonds, finely chopped
⅓ cup dried cranberries or raisins
Place cashews in a bowl. Or soak them in hot water for 10 minutes.

Drain cashews. Add to blender with with rest of the dressing ingredients. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. (Orlee used a nutribullet and it got stuck a few times so she added a dash more water to help it grind).

recipes.title: A Guide to Platter Making - Featuring Savta

items.text: Choose a big, flat platter. You can use any shape you want (e.g., round, long, oval), but round is the general go-to. If you're transferring your platter, it might be helpful if the platter has handles. (Note: Savta inherited this platter from her mother).
Choose a bed of greens, such as spinach, mixed greens, or lettuce. Cover the platter in your choice of greens.
Choose vegetables to include (e.g., big and baby carrots, cucumbers, big and baby tomatoes, red onions, scallions, radishes, baby peppers and big peppers, jicama...)
Cut the vegetables into shapes of your choice (e.g., slices, chunks...). The goal is to add as much color as you can into the platter. Savta makes some of her veggies look fancy.

Carrots - Savta peeled a carrot into strips, wrapped one around her finger and then held the circle shape in place with a toothpick. She then made a bunch and put them into ice water. Leave them in the ice water for a few hours. This will help the carrots hold the shape when the toothpicks are removed. Remove the toothpick after the carrots sit in the ice water for a while. (See pictures).

Cucumber - Score cucumbers. Take a fork and run it down the length of the cucumbers. Then cut into slices. When you cut the cucumber into slices after doing this it will now have a pretty shape around the edge. (See pictures).
Tomato centerpiece - Cut a tomato in half, make the rim look like a zig-zag crown. Stick green onions inside.
Place the vegetables in a nice pattern around the platter. Leave room in between for your proteins.
Choose your protein (e.g., scoops of tuna, scoops of egg salad, scoops of whitefish salad, scoops of copped liver, lox, salmon, balls of cream cheese, fried fish...).
Finishing touches - Add garnishes, like twisted lemon/lime slices or wedges. Maybe cut radishes into a rose shapes or crown shapes (not pictured).
Bagels/breads - Put a fancy napkin into a basket and then put the bread in. A must!

recipes.title: Lima Bean Soup

items.text: This Doda Pnena's recipe with a bit of tweaking by Ema...you know, the honey etc.
One package of dried lima beans
A few stalks of celery or 1 Anise (chopped)
5 carrots or a handful of baby carrots (chopped)
Two or three knee or marrow bones
One 8 ounce can of tomato sauce (small)
*Important: Use either “overnight” OR “quick” instructions, NOT both
Put dry lima beans into a large pot or a bowl and add 6–8 cups of cold water. Leave overnight or minimum 6 hours
Bring 6 cups cold water to a boil. Add dried lima beans and boil 2 minutes. Let sit 1-2 hours until Lima beans soften.

Drain lima beans in a colander and rinse with cold water until the water runs clear. Put aside. In a large pot, add bones and cover with water. Boil and then reduce heat to medium and continue cooking for two hours (or more if you want real bone broth).

While letting the bones cook, heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium high heat. items.text: 10 dried pitted dates or five Mejdool (large) dates
1 (16 ounce) can of Chickpeas, rinsed and drained
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, optional (I did not use)
1 (12 ounce) bag of microwave broccoli (Preferably broccoli heads) or one bag of defrosted and drained spinach
Six chicken breasts, pounded to equal thickness
Preheat oven to 350°F.Spray an 8 x 8 glass baking dish with cooking spray. If you double the recipe, use a 9 x 13 baking dish. (I don’t think it needs to be glass honestly.)
Pour hot water over the dates; cover with plastic wrap in allowed to rest for 10 minutes. Then drain the dates and chop them into small pieces.
Heat large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the Smart balance margarine.

Add garlic, then sauté for 30 seconds or until fragrant then add the dates. Sauté for another 30 seconds. Add the chickpeas, salt and pepper (If using). Sauté for another three minutes stirring frequently.
Add the broccoli (or spinach) in small batches to the chickpea mixture stirring until it is incorporated. Remove the mixture from heat and put into a bowl. Allow to cool slightly.
While the spinach or broccoli mixture is cooling, place the chicken breasts in a pan and season each with salt and pepper (if using).
Add about 2 tablespoons spinach or broccoli mixture to each pounded chicken breast. Roll the breast around the mixture. Use a toothpick if you need it to hold the filling inside the chicken.

Place the chicken side-by-side in a glass baking dish. Drizzle olive oil lightly over the tops then sprinkle the tops lightly with salt and garlic powder and paprika. Now drizzle honey over the whole thing.

Bake the chicken for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F. Remove from oven and cover the chicken with foil for five minutes. Save the additional broccoli/spinach filling to serve with the chicken.

recipes.title: Veal Roll Stuffed with Spinach and Corn Beef

items.text: Two 10 ounces of defrosted and squeezed out spinach
Two squares of defrosted sautéed onions
One or two packages of corn beef
Kitchen twine - About six or seven pieces that are about 14 inches long for tying the roast
2 T. Margarine cut into 12 small pieces
Garlic powder like 1 T. To sprinkle
1 large carrot, coarsely chopped (I used a handful of baby carrots)
1 large shallot, coarsely chopped (Instead I used for squares of defrosted sautéed onions)
2/3 cup dry white wine (I didn’t have any so I used white grape juice instead)
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Set the veal roast on a work surface, fat side up.
Cut off all the string around the roast. Open up the roast. If it’s not flat, use a very sharp knife to make cuts to make it all around the same thickness.

Mix all stuffing ingredients together well. Spread out the stuffing over the veal roast that’s been rolled out. On top of that, evenly lay out the corned beef or pastrami so that it covers most of the veal roast leaving a slight edge along the side. Roll the veal roast back up. Tie it with about six or seven pieces of kitchen twine.

Make twelve 1-inch incisions over the top of the roast and insert a piece of margarine in each hole. Rub the minced garlic over the top of the roast, then coat the meat with the remaining 1 tablespoon of margarine and sprinkle with salt, garlic and a sprinkling of paprika maybe.
Put the carrot, celery, shallot/fried onions in a 9x13 pan. Add the meat, fat side up, and drizzle the honey then olive oil on top.

Cover the pan tightly and roast the meat in the oven for 1 1/2 – 2 hours, turning it ever 30 minutes. The roast is done with an instant-read thermometer inserted in the thickest part registers 145° to 150°.

Transfer the roast to a carving board; let stand for 10 minutes. Pour the sauce through a strainer into a saucepan. Add the wine and cook over high heat/ boil until the liquid has reduced to 1 1/4 cups, abut 4 minutes. (I had a lot more gravy). Skim off the fat and season with salt and pepper.

Put two heaping tablespoons of potato starch into a cup and add a quarter cup of cold water. Mix well. Add to the sauce pan and cook until thickened. If you’re freezing the roast, put the gravy into a separate container that’s Tightly closed.)

items.text: 4 skin on bone in chicken thighs
Optional: Rice, 2 Persian cucumbers (cubed), 1 small avocado, ¼ red onion (diced), cilantro, lemon

Thinly slice 1 red onion and place slices at the base of an oven-safe dish. Grab 4 skin-on bone-in chicken thighs, dab them dry with a paper towel and add them on top of the sliced onions in the oven-safe dish. Let chicken come up to room temp while you work the sauce in the next step.

For the sauce paste, grab a medium mixing bowl. (Orlee eyeballed these measurements). Add the juice of 1 large lemon, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp olive oil, a couple generous pinches salt, pepper, 1 tbsp sweet paprika, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1/2 tbsp oregano, 1 tbsp sumac (Orlee did a little less). Mix really well.
Brush the sauce paste all over the chicken, covering all sides. Reserve some of it for later.

Put the chicken in for an initial 35 minutes in the oven at 425F. At 35 minutes remove the chicken, brush with the remaining sauce paste, and put it back in the oven for another 5 minutes. (Orlee cooked hers for longer)

Make the cucumber avocado salad by finely dicing 2 persian cucumbers, cubing 1 small avocado, finely dicing 1/4 of a small red onion (about 3 tbsp of onion), 2 tbsp fresh cilantro, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper. Give it a mix, taste, and adjust. You can also add lemon juice to this, but I left it out since the chicken was lemony enough.
Remove the chicken from the oven, plate it up with the salad to serve and top with some sumac or chile lime seasoning.
